entries.editorial_note: Prandtl Verzeichnis A no. 48, bound alone as Band XX — the parchment Prachtband with the gilt portrait-and-arms plaques, which Prandtl listed in 1932 in Harald Mortensen's collection at Copenhagen, not in Prague. Bought in Germany by professor Sigurd Wandel; Mortensen's by 1932; his gift to Det Nationalhistoriske Museum på Frederiksborg in 1950, when it was called the only Danish-owned volume from Tycho's library (Paulli & Dal 1959, p. 15); in the museum's Tycho Brahe case in 1955 (Mortensen 1955, p. 25). The museum confirmed on 28 September 2026 that the volume is inventory B3950a-b, kept in the museum library and not on display. An octavo, not a folio. Prandtl's Band XX and the Frederiksborg book are one volume; an earlier reading of Band XX as a separate Prague volume was a misreading of Prandtl. The suffix a-b names the volume (a) and the slipcase it is kept in (b), the museum's answer of 12 October 2026.
open_questions: Whether the text carries annotations in Tycho’s hand: the volume has not been searched leaf by leaf.

marks.binding: pasteboard with the year 1576 stamped into the front board; the leather covering stripped, the board later covered with paper; the library's board photographs (27 October 2026): paper-covered boards, a pale spine covering chipped and split; labels ‘T. dispersal.detail: Jesuit college at Chomutov — ‘Collegii Societatis Jesu Commotovien. catalogo inscriptus 1645’ on fol. <2>2r — and after the suppression of 1773 the University Library at the Clementinum, the route of the other Chomutov Tychoniana; how it reached Chomutov by 1645 is not recorded.

entries.editorial_note: The lead work of the incunable Sammelband 44 F 38 at the National Library, published by Boldan and Kazanskii in 2023 among incunables whose defaced provenance notes were read with a video spectral comparator: the first edition of d'Ailly's Imago mundi with his astronomical treatises, bound with the Ratdolt Euclid of 1482. ‘The owner of the Sammelband until his death in 1601 was Tycho Brahe’, shown by his autograph monogram ‘T. B.’ on the title leaf, which was supplied in manuscript at the end of the sixteenth century after the printed first leaf had been torn out, and by his glosses, for example on fol. dd1r. The two incunables may have been joined only in 1576, the year stamped into the front board; the binding is of the Uraniborg furnishing year, and the manuscript title leaf of the kind Tycho supplied to other volumes. The volume belongs to the Chomutov stratum: the college entered it in its catalogue in 1645, nine years before Gabriel Crusius's gifts to the same college. Kleinschnitzová did not list it, and it escaped every later census because it is catalogued among the incunables, outside the old-prints owner index. With the Venice Ephemerides of 1481 (Kleinschnitzová 14), the Louvain cosmography of c. 1477–1483 and the Ratdolt Euclid of 1482 are the earliest printed books now known from the library.
open_questions: Whether the manuscript title leaf and the glosses are in Tycho's hand; whether the pasteboard binding of 1576 matches the dated T. B. O. bindings; and any trace of the route from the heirs to Chomutov before 1645 — questions for the volume.

27 Oct 2026 — the binding half narrowed: the library's own photographs of the boards (Aleph MEDIA, 2833 × 3695 and 2768 × 3631 px) show both boards now covered in paper with no year, tooling or initials visible under flat light, so a die comparison with the T.B.O. 1576 bindings is impossible (the leather is gone) and only a raking-light reading of the year's figures remains; the hand half unchanged (never compared — photographs of the supplied title and fol. dd1r needed); the route half is chapter II's.
Whether the National Library's incunable collection (departments 39–44) holds further volumes with Tycho's marks: the library's former-owner index covers 1501–1800 only.
27 Oct 2026 — unchanged from any source held; an enquiry to the incunable curator (chapter IV, rank 1) is the test.

entries.title_transcribed: Liber Genethliacus sive de nativitatibus
entries.subject: Astronomy/Astrology/Mathematics

marks.inscription: the Albubater title carries ‘1671’ at the upper left (canvas 155, read 27 October 2026)
marks.annotations: Numerous annotations attributed to Tycho by Prandtl, with leaves of horoscopes and astrological tables at the end; those leaves carry a chronicle of 1535–1545 and the nativity of Andreas Schöner, cast for Nuremberg on 21 June 1530, in a hand earlier than Tycho’s, which Studnička (1901) reproduced as Tycho’s work; re-read 27 October 2026: the diary (canvas 303) and the nativity (canvas 304, ‘Anno M·D·X·X·X·[X]’ with the fourth X overwritten; Dies martis = 1530) in the Schöner hand; later layers on canvases 246 and 314 not compared

entries.editorial_note: Prandtl Verzeichnis A no.1; bound in Band IV. Prandtl records numerous annotations in Tycho's hand, with leaves of horoscopes and astrological tables at the end. The attribution is Prandtl's, and it is not exhaustive: at least one pre-Tycho hand is also present in the volume, whose terminal leaves carry a personal chronicle headed Accidentia mea, dated 1535–1545, and a nativity headed natus Andreas Schoenerus, cast for Nuremberg on 21 June 1530 (dies Martis, as the figure says; reproduced by Studnička 1901, Bericht, p. 22, as Tycho's work) — both antedating Tycho's birth on 14 December 1546. Studnička read the cost note on the first leaf of the manuscript once bound in the volume, which lists the Gauricus, the Albubater, the Cardanus and the binder’s fee, as Tycho’s own account of the purchase and the binding (Bericht, pp. 20–21), and Kleinschnitzová read the binding instruction on the last leaf of the Glareanus 19 G 20, which names the Gauricus and the Albubater, as Tycho’s hand (1933, no. 42, p. 93); the cost note is headed with Schöner’s name. Whose hands the volume’s annotations are has not been established by a comparison of hands. Grade set on 20 October 2026 under the document rule (a surviving copy with his marks, or a document naming the book as his, is A; a dedication, the 1642 note alone or a queried mark is B; a third party's report or the compiler's inference is C).

entries.title_transcribed: Tabulae Alphonsinae (edition unknown)
entries.subject: Astronomy

acquisition.channel: bought — Dreyer 1890, p. 18; Šolc 2006, p. 190

entries.editorial_note: The Alphonsine Tables Tycho procured in his Leipzig student years beside the Prutenic Tables: Dreyer 1890, p. 18 (‘he did not long content himself with the use of the Ephemerides of Stadius, but procured the Alphonsine tables and the Prutenic tables’); Šolc 2006, printed p. 190 (scan 4), dates the purchase ‘later (1564) at Leipzig’ and pairs it with the surviving Prutenic copy 14 J 192 (Soupis 20), whose identification with the 1564 purchase is his, the copy carrying no provenance note; the loci record of the Leipzig years places the acquisition at Leipzig at stay precision. Edition unknown; status ghost; grade B on Dreyer's statement, which rests on Tycho's own comparison of the 1563 conjunction with both tables (ownership rather than loan is the inference). Distinct from the Venice 1492 edition with Lave Urne's dedication of 1590 at TU Wien (the Vienna copy entered from Mortensen) and from the Paris 1553 edition Herwart sent in December 1600.

entries.title_transcribed: Tabulae Alphonsinae
entries.subject: Astronomy/Tables

marks.inscription: many Tycho autograph notes; title-page dedication to Tycho dated 1590 from Lave Urne til Bæltebjærg

entries.editorial_note: The Alphonsine Tables at the Technische Universität Wien (Tresor 7704 I), heavily annotated by Tycho and dedicated to him in 1590 by Lave Urne til Bæltebjærg, landsdommer in Skåne; formerly in the Prague Jesuit College (Mortensen 1955, p. 30). The volume is distinct from the Paris edition of 1553 of the Tables that Herwart von Hohenburg sent Tycho from Munich on 10 December 1600, a copy marked ‘No. 43’ (Opera omnia VIII, pp. 393–394: ‘mitto Alphonsinas Tabulas recognitas, Parisijs A° 53 impressas, No. 43 signatas’). Norlind (1970, p. 337) prints the title-page notes: ‘Collegij Caesarei Societatis Iesu Pragae. I Bibl. min. Anno 1642. Ex Bibliotheca Tichoniana’ above the title, and below it ‘Hunc librum dono dedj singularj Amico meo Domino Tychoni Brahe de Knudstorp Amicitiae ergo Anno salutis 1590. Laue Vrne senior min hand’. Tycho’s notes and the Urne dedication are known from Teichl’s report to Mortensen and from the title-page inscriptions Norlind prints; neither describes the notes, and the library’s own record names no former owner. Grade set on 20 October 2026 under the document rule (a surviving copy with his marks, or a document naming the book as his, is A; a dedication, the 1642 note alone or a queried mark is B; a third party's report or the compiler's inference is C). Lave (Lauge) Urne the elder, of Belteberga, landsdommer in Skåne from 1589, lived 1535/39 – 8 October 1623 (DBL), not to 1625 as Mortensen 1955 and the earlier record have it; the copy is not ‘the only one of this edition in Austria’ — GW 1258 (ISTC ia00535000) lists six other Austrian copies. The inscription in full: ‘Hunc librum dono dedj singularj Amico meo / Domino Tychoni Brahe de Knudstorp Amicitiae ergo / Anno salutis 1590. Laue urne senior / min hand.’ — the only dated presentation copy to Tycho known; reported by Teichl 1943 (Mortensen 1955, p. 30), transcribed by Norlind 1970 p. 337; not examined since; the TU Wien record carries no provenance (register dossier of 27 October 2026, §16-04).
open_questions: What Tycho’s annotations in the volume contain: they are known only from Teichl’s report to Mortensen (1955, p. 30) and from the title-page inscriptions Norlind prints (1970, p. 337), neither of which describes them, and the library’s record of Tresor 7704 I names no former owner; an examination of the volume would settle it.

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 16; NK Clementinum Sign. 14 J 28, in the original brown binding with the initials ‘T. B. O. 1580’ (Kleinschnitzová; Norlind 1970, p. 337). Regiomontanus’s Oratio introductoria and Melanchthon’s prefatory letter, which Šolc 2002 (p. 330) lists for the volume, are the front matter of the Nuremberg edition of 1537, not separate works. Tycho owned this edition and wanted a better text: he complained in August 1598 that the Latin translation teemed with errors (Opera omnia VIII, 102), asked Scaliger for the Arabic in April 1599 (VIII, 152), heard in March 1600 that Scaliger had neither it nor another Latin version (VIII, 264), and in November 1600 was offered a copy of the edition of 1537 by Herwart von Hohenburg (VIII, 386) (Norlind 1970, p. 337).

norlind.ownership_verdict: located copy, Prague (Kl. nr 16; original binding with initials T. B. O. 1580); Tycho owned the 1537 edition but sought the Arabic text or a better Latin translation (letters 1598-1600)
norlind.discussion: Originalbd med initialerna »T. B. O. 1580». – Albategnius' skrift, som f.ö. också utgavs separat, innehåller endast texten till hans berömda tabeller, vilka bl.a. upptogo stjärnpositioner för epoken 879,0. Texten är översatt av Plato från Tivoli med tillägg av Regiomontanus. Den arabiska texten återutgavs med latinsk översättning först av Nallino 1903–07. – Tycho skriver till Scaliger i april 1599 (VIII, 152), att han önskade den arabiska texten. Redan i aug. 1598 (VIII, 102) hade han klagat över, att den latinska översättningen vimlade av fel. Som svar på Tychos brev från april 1599, meddelar Scaliger, mars 1600 (VIII, 264), att han inte kunnat komma över någon arabisk text och f.n. inte har någon latinsk översättning. Tycho hänvände sig tydligen därefter till Herwart von Hohenburg i München. I nov. 1600 (VIII, 386) svarar denne, att uppl. 1537 är svår att skaffa och f.ö. betingar ett högt pris; den är inkorrekt på flera ställen. Ett exemplar har han emellertid förvärvat från ett bibliotek och han erbjuder sig att skicka det. Tycho, som dock ägde denna uppl., synes ha trott, att det skulle ha funnits ytterligare en latinsk översättning. En sådan existerade emellertid icke vid denna tid.

entries.author_identified: Angelus, Johannes (with Jacobus Angelus, De cometis)
entries.title_transcribed: Astrolabium planum; bound/sent with Jacobus Angelus, De cometis
entries.subject: Astronomy/Instruments
entries.editorial_note: Herwart von Hohenburg sent Tycho Johannes Angelus’s Astrolabium planum together with Jacobus Angelus’s De cometis with his letter of 27 November 1600 (‘IOANNIS ANGELI Astrolabium et Planum cum IACOBO ANGELO de Cometis... mitto’). Whether a gift or simply a consignment, it is distinct from the Bavarian loans: no library catalogue number is given for it, and the book was therefore Tycho’s own. Grade set on 20 October 2026 under the document rule (a surviving copy with his marks, or a document naming the book as his, is A; a dedication, the 1642 note alone or a queried mark is B; a third party's report or the compiler's inference is C).

entries.title_transcribed: Astronomicum Caesareum
entries.subject: Astronomy/Astrology/Mathematics

marks.inscription: Tycho's dated motto entry of 14 June 1599 on the blank leaf after the arms — of the album kind, not an ownership mark

entries.editorial_note: Prandtl Verzeichnis A no. 2, bound as Band VI. The attestation is the inscription alone: a dated motto entry written on the day Tycho left Wittenberg, which proves that he held the book and wrote in it, not that it was his. Norlind doubted the ownership; the Gotha library reads the entry as a gift to Duke Friedrich Wilhelm of Saxe-Weimar. See the volume record. Status kept at located, B, on 20 October 2026 with the doubt standing here: the only Tycho evidence is the dated motto entry of 14 June 1599, of the album kind; Norlind doubted the ownership and the Gotha copy record names Duke Friedrich Wilhelm as recipient.
open_questions: Whether the book was Tycho's own before 14 June 1599 or Duke Friedrich Wilhelm's book in which he wrote; the basis of the Gotha copy record's naming of the duke as recipient (probably Gehrt 2013 on the duke's library); and the sense of Rauch's remark that the book came to Gotha from Munich.

norlind.discussion:
Ett astronomiskt praktverk med rörliga pappskivor till åskådliggörande av planeternas rörelser. »Ouvrage très intéressant pour connaître l'état de l'astronomie vers le milieu du XVIe siècle» (Houzeau & Lancaster); »the most sumptuous scientific book ever printed» (D. J. Price, »The equatories of the planetis», Cambr. 1955, s. 132). Dåtidens omdöme om verket S. A. Ionides, »Caesar's Astronomy», i: »Osiris» 1936, s. 356–389.
Ett astronomiskt praktverk med rörliga pappskivor till åskådliggörande av planeternas rörelser. »Ouvrage très intéressant pour connaître l'état de l'astronomie vers le milieu du XVIe siècle» (Houzeau & Lancaster); »the most sumptuous scientific book ever printed» (D. J. Price, »The equatories of the planetis», Cambr. 1955, s. 132). Dåtidens omdöme om verket var emellertid ganska kritiskt. Hagecius skriver sålunda till Tycho i nov. 1588 (VII, 147): »Hunc eruditum pulverem, in quo nos versamur, ille [sc. Apianus] ne somniavit quidem. Eius artem sæpe Rheticus, bonæ memoriæ, vocare solitus erat faden Dunst.» Kepler beklagar i sin »De motibus stellæ Martis», kap. 14, den »miserabilem industriam» som Apianus nedlagt på sitt verk, men han menar ändå, att Apianus »palmam ... inde famæ perennis est adeptus, quicquid operibus ipsis fortuna ista detrimenti attulerit».
Tycho ägde i varje fall ett exemplar (till Hagecius nov. 1589; VII, 212). Längre fram i brevet (215) omtalar han ett annat exemplar, som han en gång köpte för 20 fl. och sedermera skänkte Paul Wittich vid dennes besök på Hven 1580. Tycho ber nu Hagecius att, eftersom Wittich avlidit, underhandla med systern i Tychos namn angående förvärvande av dennes bibliotek, som tydligen måste ha varit synnerligen värdefullt. Lyckas Hagecius i sina underhandlingar, skall han få det exemplar, som Wittich erhöll av Tycho. – I Landesbibliothek i Gotha finnes ett exemplar, däri Tycho på ett tomt blad i början gjort en del anteckningar (se Chr. Rausch i: Zeitschr. f. Bücherfreunde, N.F. 5: 2, 1914, s. 223–224). De utgöras av några verser ur Davids 19:e psalm (»Cœli enarrant Gloriam Dei et opera manuum eius annunciat firmamentum») samt ett distikon: »Qui negat esse Deum cœlos et sidera spectet / Esse etenim monstrat stella vel una Deum.» Därunder: »Tycho Brahe / scripsi / Anno 1599 / Junii die 14 / quo Viteberga / discessi / Pragam / a Cæsare vocatus.»
Pr. upptager exemplaret som tillhörigt Tycho (nr 1 i hans förteckning). Att det skulle ha varit Tychos, synes dock knappast sannolikt. Den handskrivna anteckningen påminner snarare om en stamboksautograf. Exemplaret kan mycket väl ha tillhört någon annan, kanske rent av hertig Fredrik Wilhelm av Sachsen-Altenburg, med vilken Tycho vid denna tid stod i förbindelse.
Ortroy, Apianus förtecknar under nr 112 ett 30-tal kända exemplar. marks.inscription: Tycho's presentation inscription to Paul Wittich, Hven, 29 October 1580: 'D[omi]no Paulo Witichio Wratislauiensj ob amicitam & comune[m] mathemati[cum] amorem d[ono] d[edit] Tÿcho Brahe Huanae anno 1580 29 Octobris.'
marks.annotations: former owners' manuscript annotations in two hands with underscoring, a manuscript pagination 1–46 from p. [2], some initials hand-coloured by a former owner (the library's record, read 6 October 2026); hands unattributed, no image held
marks.binding: half leather and marbled paper over boards, an armorial device pasted to the front cover, the date 1686 tooled on it, fabric ties (one missing) — not Tycho's binding (the library's record; 'German half calf; dated 1686', the Schaffner catalogue of 1977)

entries.editorial_note: Now at the University of Chicago Library (Schaffner bequest, 1972; bib 146807). Tycho's gift to Wittich at his departure from Hven, inscribed 29 October 1580; Tycho had paid 20 florins for it and told Hagecius on 1 November 1589 that he did not reclaim it and had another copy to hand (TBOO VII, 212 and 215; Gingerich's benchmark of an expensive book against about one florin for a De revolutionibus, Annotated Census, p. xv). The book left Tycho's library by gift in his lifetime and never returned; the identification of the Chicago copy rests on the library's own catalogue of 1977 (entry 15) and exhibit page. See the volume record.
open_questions: The owners between Wittich's sister at Wrocław and Louis H. Silver: the binding of 1686 is the only fixed point; Gingerich's survey of copies (Röttel 1995), the Sotheby's catalogue of 8–9 November 1965 (lot 4) and the Newberry's 1964 handlist of the Silver collection should carry the line.

The two annotating hands the record notes, and the underscoring: whether either is Wittich's (his annotated copies of De revolutionibus would serve for comparison) or Tycho's; and the readings 'amicitam' and 'Huanae' in the record's transcription of the inscription. Images of the title page and of the annotated leaves would settle it.

norlind.discussion:
Ett astronomiskt praktverk med rörliga pappskivor till åskådliggörande av planeternas rörelser. »Ouvrage très intéressant pour connaître l'état de l'astronomie vers le milieu du XVIe siècle» (Houzeau & Lancaster); »the most sumptuous scientific book ever printed» (D. J. Price, »The equatories of the planetis», Cambr. 1955, s. 132). Dåtidens omdöme om verket S. A. Ionides, »Caesar's Astronomy», i: »Osiris» 1936, s. 356–389.
Ett astronomiskt praktverk med rörliga pappskivor till åskådliggörande av planeternas rörelser. »Ouvrage très intéressant pour connaître l'état de l'astronomie vers le milieu du XVIe siècle» (Houzeau & Lancaster); »the most sumptuous scientific book ever printed» (D. J. Price, »The equatories of the planetis», Cambr. 1955, s. 132). Dåtidens omdöme om verket var emellertid ganska kritiskt. Hagecius skriver sålunda till Tycho i nov. 1588 (VII, 147): »Hunc eruditum pulverem, in quo nos versamur, ille [sc. Apianus] ne somniavit quidem. Eius artem sæpe Rheticus, bonæ memoriæ, vocare solitus erat faden Dunst.» Kepler beklagar i sin »De motibus stellæ Martis», kap. 14, den »miserabilem industriam» som Apianus nedlagt på sitt verk, men han menar ändå, att Apianus »palmam ... inde famæ perennis est adeptus, quicquid operibus ipsis fortuna ista detrimenti attulerit».
Tycho ägde i varje fall ett exemplar (till Hagecius nov. 1589; VII, 212). Längre fram i brevet (215) omtalar han ett annat exemplar, som han en gång köpte för 20 fl. och sedermera skänkte Paul Wittich vid dennes besök på Hven 1580. Tycho ber nu Hagecius att, eftersom Wittich avlidit, underhandla med systern i Tychos namn angående förvärvande av dennes bibliotek, som tydligen måste ha varit synnerligen värdefullt. Lyckas Hagecius i sina underhandlingar, skall han få det exemplar, som Wittich erhöll av Tycho. – I Landesbibliothek i Gotha finnes ett exemplar, däri Tycho på ett tomt blad i början gjort en del anteckningar (se Chr. Rausch i: Zeitschr. f. Bücherfreunde, N.F. 5: 2, 1914, s. 223–224). De utgöras av några verser ur Davids 19:e psalm (»Cœli enarrant Gloriam Dei et opera manuum eius annunciat firmamentum») samt ett distikon: »Qui negat esse Deum cœlos et sidera spectet / Esse etenim monstrat stella vel una Deum.» Därunder: »Tycho Brahe / scripsi / Anno 1599 / Junii die 14 / quo Viteberga / discessi / Pragam / a Cæsare vocatus.»
Pr. upptager exemplaret som tillhörigt Tycho (nr 1 i hans förteckning). Att det skulle ha varit Tychos, synes dock knappast sannolikt. Den handskrivna anteckningen påminner snarare om en stamboksautograf. Exemplaret kan mycket väl ha tillhört någon annan, kanske rent av hertig Fredrik Wilhelm av Sachsen-Altenburg, med vilken Tycho vid denna tid stod i förbindelse.

entries.source: Gingerich 2002 (Recent Notes on Tycho Brahe's Library)
entries.title_transcribed: Astronomicum Caesareum (Ingolstadt, 1540), bound with Johann Schöner's equatorium of 1521
entries.subject: Astronomy/Instruments

acquisition.date: by 1583 (the year stamped on the binding with Tycho's initials)

marks.annotations: Several annotations by Tycho, all in the comet section near the end of the Astronomicum Caesareum (Gingerich 2002, p. 328); fig. 2 reproduces a detail of f. O1 verso, where a marginal heading beside Apianus's table of the comet's daily motion reads, in the reproduction, ‘Motus diurnus Cometae in suo circulo’, with a second short note below it and a longer note in the outer margin. Later annotations in other hands: the star names on the planisphere written in French; on the facing page a note partly in Dutch and partly in Flemish
marks.binding: Binding stamped with the initials ‘T.B.O.’ above the date ‘1583’ (Gingerich 2002, p. 328, from the owner's enquiry); not otherwise described

dispersal.detail: The French and Dutch/Flemish annotations place the volume around Antwerp or Brussels for a very long time; until about 1960 it was in a monastery library there. Gingerich's suggestion: it migrated to the Low Countries by the same Jesuit hands that carried the Wittich Copernicus now in Liège.

entries.editorial_note: Tycho’s own retained Astronomicum Caesareum, bound for him in 1583 with Schöner’s equatorium of 1521 and stamped ‘T.B.O. 1583’; he gave a second copy to Paul Wittich (Chicago) and inscribed a third at Wittenberg on 14 June 1599 (Gotha, Prandtl Band VI). The volume surfaced about 2000 through an e-mail enquiry to Gingerich from its Belgian owner, who asked why books of 1521 and 1540 sat in a binding stamped 1583 with the initials TBO; Gingerich recognised the mark and learned of Tycho’s annotations in the comet section (2002, pp. 327–328, fig. 2 = f. O1 verso). Later annotations in French and in Dutch or Flemish place the volume around Antwerp or Brussels for a long period, in a monastery library until about 1960 — in Gingerich’s view carried there by the same Jesuit hands as the Wittich Copernicus now in Liège. It was sold about 2001–2002 to an anonymous American collector for, Gingerich reports, close to a million dollars. Gingerich (2002, p. 327) had known only the Wittich copy and presumed that Tycho had retained another, which he had not found among the more than a hundred copies he had examined. Tycho himself attests a second Astronomicum Caesareum at Hven in 1589: offering Hagecius the Wittich copy for his trouble, he wrote on 1 November 1589 that he did not want it back, ‘as I have another copy at hand’ (Opera omnia VII, pp. 214–215; Gingerich and Westman 1988, p. 21) — this volume, bound six years earlier, not the Gotha copy inscribed in 1599.
open_questions: Which monastery in the Low Countries held the volume until about 1960, who the Belgian owner of about 2000 was, and who bought it in about 2001–2002: Gingerich names none of them, and the dealer’s or the owner’s records would.
Which edition of Schöner’s equatorium of 1521 is bound with the Apianus: Gingerich gives neither title nor imprint, and a description of the volume would settle it.

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 42:2: ‘Kein Tychonianum’. Bound at the Clementinum into the composite 19 G 20 with works of other provenance; only the Glareanus, with Tycho’s binder’s instruction on its last leaf, is his. Entered so that the work is not claimed for the library from its shelfmark. Šolc 2006 (printed p. 190 (scan 4)) counts ‘one more copy of this title, Antwerp 1545’ as being in the Bibliotheca Tychoniana fund, with ‘a different history’ — bound ‘with further Tycho prints’ into the convolute only later in the Clementinum (Soupis 42, 19 G 20). Kleinschnitzová's verdict, ‘Kein Tychonianum’, stands here: Šolc names no copy-specific ground, and by his own rule of p. 189 ‘the fund’ is the Soupis-numbered set of volumes.

entries.subject: Astronomy/Astrology/Mathematics

acquisition.place: Copenhagen — inferred from the binding’s year 1561 and Tycho’s departure from Denmark on 14 February 1562; no source names the place
acquisition.channel: bought as a student with the Regiomontanus in the same volume: the purchase note ‘Eptg [emptus] thalero & 4 Groshj’ stands on the volume’s fly-title and the binding is stamped ‘Anno 1561’ (Prandtl 1932, Band II; Klem, Årbog 1957, p. 8)

marks.inscription: the ownership inscriptions and the purchase note stand on the fly-title of the Regiomontanus, first in the volume
marks.annotations: fol. 53r–v: four places with their positions in an early hand, read by the museum as ‘Elzingborgum 35 46. 57 0 / Lunda Lundt 36 30 57 23 / Vesby Gotlandiæ 47 5. 59 50 / Rumefalche [?] 46 35 60 15’. The Helsingborg and Lund figures are the book's own printed values from the Scania table on fol. 41v (‘Elseburgum 35 46 | 57 0’, ‘Lundis vel Lunda 36 30 | 57 23’), transcribed beside the printed Zealand–Scania island entry; Visby and the fourth place, which the printed table lacks, stand beside the Gotland entry on fol. 53v, so the fourth place was taken for a Gotland or neighbouring-island locality; it is Schöner's ‘Rumefalche’ (Luculentissima quaedam terrae totius descriptio, 1515, fo. 34r: ‘Bespue 47.5.59.50. Rumefalche 46.35.60.15.’), a Clavus-derived pseudo-toponym of Gotland from the Ulm Ptolemy of 1486 (Bjørnbo and Petersen 1904, pp. 115, 118), identified 21 October 2026. The latitudes are the Ptolemaic values Tycho later corrected (Helsingborg 56 3, Lund 55 45: TBOO V, 309–312), so the entries predate his Danish latitude programme; the hand is undated and uncompared. Photographed 20 October 2026: the four lines are in one ink and ductus — ‘Elzingborgum’ with a superscript c above the name, ‘Lunda’, ‘Vesbÿ Gotlandiæ’, and a fourth whose letters read R-?-n-s-f-a-l-?-h-?; read again on 21 October 2026 as ‘Lůnda lůndt’, ‘Veſbÿ Gotlandiæ’ and ‘Rumefalche’ (the museum's reading stands; the tall letter is an f), the u-marks and the diaeresis being the writer's habit; Visby and Rumefalche are Schöner's two Gotland ‘cities’ with his figures, Helsingborg and Lund his figures as Apian reprinted them. Also by hand: ‘Octava sphaera’ at the ring of the Schema praemissae divisionis, and ‘Wittenberga’ underlined in the German place table
marks.binding: Band II: brown calf, blind-ruled mirror panels on both boards, originally gilt floral stamps, TVCHO BRADE stamped on the front board, ANNO 1561 on the rear, three raised bands; on the spine the remnant of a label with a library shelfmark 204 (the museum's record, 1957:0030)

entries.editorial_note: Prandtl Verzeichnis A no. 3; bound in Band II. The volume is at M/S Museet for Søfart, Helsingør, inventory 1957:0030, the gift of Lia and Oscar Ekman in 1957. The museum’s record gives the Paris 1553 title with the colophon dated 1551, fol. 1–74, the cordiform map inserted between fol. 34 and 35, and the four added positions on fol. 53r–v. The volume is in the museum’s own keeping; the Royal Library deposit reported in 1987 and 1992 has ended (the museum’s confirmation of 13 October 2026). Gingerich 2002 (p. 325) still recorded ‘a copy of the 1561 edition of Petrus Apianus’ Cosmographia’ as sold by a Munich antiquariat to an undisclosed location: this is the present volume, whose binding is stamped 1561. Examined at the museum on 20 October 2026: the four places read on the leaf, the herbarium confirmed, the accession note read. The fol. 53 lines read letter by letter on 21 October 2026; the hand compared with the Graphonomicon's dated specimens (inconclusive). The fourth place identified on 21 October 2026 as Schöner's Rumefalche (1515, fo. 34r), Clavus's pseudo-toponym; the misreading of its fifth letter in the transcription withdrawn. Reviewed on 29 October 2026: of the six volumes the house has carried as the student’s, this is the one documented as Tycho’s before he left Denmark on 14 February 1562 — by the boards stamped with his name and the year 1561, and by nothing else: the purchase note and the ownership entries are undated, and no hand in the volume is attributed. Copenhagen as the place of purchase is an inference from the year (the Kronik of 1987 read the Leipzig register’s ‘16 October 1561’ as the matriculation; it is the winter-semester heading, Norlind 1970, p. 16, and Tycho and Vedel matriculated in the spring of 1562); the price in thaler and groschen is German money of account, which no source explains for a Copenhagen purchase; Klem’s ‘i 1561’ (Årbog 1957, p. 8) is the binding’s year, not the note’s. The volume came back to Denmark as Oscar Ekman’s bequest, entered in January 1957 by his widow Lia in the dead man’s name (he died 16 September 1956; the sale catalogue of 1965, lot 497: ‘according to the last will of ingeniør Ekman’, not for sale).

entries.title_transcribed: Conicorum libri IV (prob. Commandino, Bologna 1566; or Memmo, Venice 1537)
entries.subject: Mathematics
entries.editorial_note: Norlind (1970, pp. 338–339): ‘Vi veta, att biblioteket på Hven ägde ett exemplar av Apollonius’ verk (Bil. 6)’ — the library on Hven owned a copy, on the evidence of his Bilaga 6. Which of the two Latin translations it was, Memmo’s (Venice 1537) or Commandino’s (Bologna 1566, with Eutocius’s commentary), is not known; Norlind inclines to Commandino’s. The ‘Opera’ that Herwart von Hohenburg sent from Munich at Tycho’s request in September 1600 (Opera omnia VIII, 366) was a loan, its title that of the edition of 1537. Christian Hansen Riber’s deposition of 13/23 May 1598 adds the one witness to the shelf: the former students, ‘who examined your library whenever we liked’, attest that it never held any writing of Apollonius on hypotheses and that Tycho had no book of his but the Conics (Jardine & Segonds 2008, p. 169). The authors suppose that Kepler found the Commandino volume, which also carries Serenus, in Tycho’s library for the Contra Ursum, and conjecture that the ‘Apollonij Pergaei Opera’ Herwart sent on 23 September 1600 may be the copy Kepler used; their page prints the editions as Memmo 1527 and Commandino 1556, misprints for 1537 and 1566 (pp. 169–170 n. 4).

norlind.discussion: Av detta berömda verk funnos vid denna tid tvenne latinska översättningar (av bok I–IV, som äro de enda bevarade på grekiska; bok V–VII föreligga endast i arabisk övers.). Den ena översättningen av den venetianske patriciern Johannes Baptista Memus utgavs i Venedig 1537.2°. Den viktigaste var dock av Federicus Commandinus och den trycktes i Bologna 1566, 2°. Den innehåller bl.a. Eutocius' kommentar och var det första försöket att göra verket begripligt genom förklarande noter. Vi veta, att biblioteket på Hven ägde ett exemplar av Apollonius' verk (Bil. 6), men vilken upplaga det varit, är icke känt; man skulle emellertid med skäl kunna gissa på Commandinus' översättning. – I sept. 1600 (VIII, 366) skickade Herwart från München på Tychos begäran till låns Apollonius' »Opera», detta är titeln på den upplaga, som trycktes 1537. föreligga endast i arabisk övers.). entries.title_transcribed: De natura caeli triplicis libelli tres
entries.subject: Cosmology

acquisition.channel: the author’s dedication to Tycho; a presentation copy is presumed, none is documented (Norlind 1970, p. 339)

entries.editorial_note: Cort Aslakssøn (Cunradus Aslacus, Cort Axelsen; Bergen 1564–1624), Tycho’s famulus on Hven 1590–93 and later the first Norwegian professor at Copenhagen. Full title: De natura caeli triplicis libelli tres, quorum I. de caelo aëreo, II. de caelo sidereo, III. de caelo perpetuo, e sacrarum litterarum & praestantium philosophorum thesauris concinnati (Siegen [Sigenae Nassoviorum]: Christoph Rab, Christophorus Corvinus, 1597). VD16 A 3899; Zinner 3699; [7] leaves and 214 pages, octavo (VD16; the ‘4°’ at Norlind, p. 339, is an error). Written and printed while Aslakssøn was abroad as tutor to Otto Brahe (matriculated at Basel 1596/97). The book is dedicated to Tycho (Norlind, p. 339; Store norske leksikon), whence Norlind’s inference that it ‘har väl alltså befunnit sig i Tychos bibliotek’. The ownership rests on that inference alone: no copy with Tycho’s marks and no presentation copy is recorded in the inventories of Prandtl, Kleinschnitzová, Šolc or Mortensen, or in the trade. In the preface Aslakssøn declares for Copernicus, a position Tycho rejected, so that the dedication stands in tension with the book’s own position. The work is a ‘Mosaic physics’, a synthesis of astronomy and scripture on the three heavens (elemental or aerial, astronomical or sidereal, eternal or perpetual); Comenius later listed Aslakssøn among the Mosaic physicists who preceded him. Book III, De caelo perpetuo, was translated into English as ‘The Description of Heaven … Composed in Latine by Cunradus Aslachus, and conuerted into English by Raph [Ralph] Iennings’ (London 1623; EEBO A22193). Copies of the edition survive in Munich (Bayerische Staatsbibliothek), Vienna (Österreichische Nationalbibliothek) and Copenhagen (Royal Library); none is Tycho’s. The dedicatory epistle, read in the Munich copy, is addressed ‘Tychoni Brahe de Knudstrup, fundatori Arcis Uraniburgicae … sideralis scientiae scrutatori, instauratori, conservatori unico’, dated Basel, 16 November 1596, and signed ‘Cunradus Aslachus Bergensis’; it hails Tycho as ‘indefessus Caeli scrutator & Atlas’ and pays eyewitness homage to his celestial globe and astronomical instruments.

dedication.content: Offers the book as 'primitiae' / a 'gratae recordationis symbolum' in return for Tycho's benefactions; hails him as 'indefessus ille Caeli scrutator & Atlas'; praises the Brahe family's nobility and Tycho's heroic-Herculean labours in sidereal science, his celestial Globe ('Globus ille caelestis, infinitis tuis lucubrationibus & vigiliis comparatus, Mundoque pridem concessus') and his astronomical instruments ('Machinae Astronomicae tua opera incredibili sumptu affabré elaboratae'). The preface (sig. A2v) thanks his Siegen/Herborn teachers Johannes Piscator and Johann Bisterfeld, and records submitting the work to Rudolph Goclenius the Elder at the Frankfurt fair; it defends views 'a communi scholarum opinione abhorrentia' (the cautiously-stated Copernican paradoxes). A separate epigram 'Ad authorem' by Johannes Piscator faces the title.

entries.title_transcribed: De medendis humani corporis malis Enchiridion

acquisition.channel: bought as a student — if the cipher is Tycho’s (ownership C): the pigskin binding of the volume is blind-stamped ‘T. B. 1560’ and the Bayrus bound first in it is printed in 1560 (Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 47; Christianson 1967, pp. 200–201); no inscription, annotation or Jesuit note of 1642 supports it

marks.inscription: the professed house's ‘Dom[us] Professa[e] Soc: JESV ad S. Nic: Prag[ae] / Catal: … inscript. / Lit.’ on the Bayrus title (Šolc 2018 fig. 1c, read 27 October 2026)
marks.binding: light leather, blind-tooled: roll border of medallion heads; front board T [ornament] B in the upper compartment (no O), a half-length figured panel, the year below not legible on Šolc 2018 fig. 1a; rear board a figured panel with an inscription beginning ‘CASTA’, label ‘Tres. M 47’ (fig. 1b)

entries.editorial_note:
Kleinschnitzová 1933 no.47; NK Clementinum Sign. 18 J 318. The library's record for 18 J 318 gives the imprint as Basel, Petrus Perna, 1560 (the survivor record for 18 J 318; Norlind p. 339 ‘Basileæ 1560’), and Šolc's Czech text of 2006 (p. 190) prints ‘Basileae 1560’; his German text of 1999 (§ 2.528, printed p. 149) prints ‘Basel 1559’, the year of the Macer bound with it — a slip, not a second edition, unless the title page says otherwise. The pressed ‘T. B. 1560’ of the binding is the year of the purchase in either case. The ‘T. B. 1560’ volume is the earliest dated binding of Tycho’s and, while the purchase note of the Ptolemy 5 B 70 is disputed, the earliest book securely his (Christianson 1967, pp. 200–201: ‘two of his own “textbooks”’).

Ownership graded B on 28 October 2026: the attribution rests on the blind-stamped cipher T·B and the year 1560 on the binding alone — no inscription, no annotation, no 1642 or Chomutov mark, and Kleinschnitzová 1933 gives no argument. The cipher is consistent with Tycho's documented series of initial-and-year bindings 1561–1583 (Helsingør 1561, Uppsala 1563, Strahov and 10 G 47 1567, T.B.O. 1576–1583) and the contents fit the Copenhagen curriculum of 1560, but T·B alone identifies no one. The NK ČR photographs requested on 28 October 2026 (the three edges, both boards, the three title pages at 600 dpi) and an EBDB identification of the panel stamps are the tests.

Reviewed again on 29 October 2026, the literature pack read whole: ownership graded C (was B). Beyond the cipher the literature holds nothing — no inscription, no annotation, no hand, no note of 1642. Kleinschnitzová (1933, pp. 76–78) herself sets the volume outside the twenty-three Clementinum volumes that carry the note of 1642 and says it ‘verirrt sich’, strayed, into the Jesuit professed house on the Malá Strana — an explanation that assumes what it should show; Norlind’s ‘T. B. O. 1560’ (1970, p. 339) reads a letter the board does not carry; the library’s record gives Tycho the year 1567 in its former-owner field without a basis; Šolc (1999, 2006, 2018), Christianson (1967, 2020), Thoren and Pařez all derive from Kleinschnitzová. If the cipher is Tycho’s, the year 1560 places the binding before his departure from Denmark; whether it is Tycho’s is the whole question, and the National Library’s photographs are the test. Decided on 29 October 2026.

entries.title_transcribed: Diversarum speculationum mathematicarum et physicarum liber
entries.subject: Astronomy/Astrology/Mathematics
entries.editorial_note: Norlind 1970, p. 340: that Tycho owned a copy of some edition is probable, since the Progymnasmata (Opera omnia III, pp. 251–253) quote verbatim a letter of Benedetti to Raimondo of Verona against the view that the new star of 1572 was one of Cassiopeia’s stars; which edition cannot be settled (in the Turin edition of 1585 the letter stands at pp. 371–374). No copy, receipt or mark is recorded; no edition is specified, and no mark by which a copy of Tycho’s could be recognised is known.

norlind.entry: Benedictus, Johannes Baptista: Diversarum speculationum mathematicarum et physicarum liber.
norlind.ownership_verdict: probably owned, edition unknown (quoted verbatim in Progymnasmata; also cited in a letter to Rothmann 1589)
norlind.discussion: Att Tycho ägt ett exemplar av någon upplaga av detta verk, är sannolikt. I »Prog.» (III, 251–253) citerar han ordagrant ett ställe härur, ur ett brev från Benedictus till Raimundus från Verona, vari denne polemiserar mot Raimundus' åsikt, att den nya stjärnan i Cassiopeia icke vore »ny» utan en av stjärnorna där. Av Tychos ord framgår, att boken varit sällsynt. Vilken upplaga det varit, kan icke fastslås med säkerhet. I upplagan, tryckt i Torino 1585, 2°, står brevet på s. 371–374 (jfr G. Bordiga, »Giovanni Battista Benedetti», i: »Atti del R. Ist. Veneto di scienze» etc., 85, 1925–26, s. 613). Riccardi, »Biblioteca matematica italiana» uppger första upplagan tryckt i Torino 1580 och känner ingen upplaga från 1585 (endast ett omtryck av uppl. 1580). I ett brev till Rothmann, febr. 1589 (VI, 172) nämner Tycho ett annat brev från Benedictus (s. 256–257 i nyssnämnda upplaga) vari behandlas bl.a. månens ljus, Benedictus menar sålunda, att det sekundära ljuset förorsakas av planeten Venus – en åsikt som Tycho trodde sig ha bekräftat genom sina egna observationer.

Johannes Schmidt sending the book to a nobleman he addresses as Smil — ‘Promissum transmitto librum, Doctissime Smile … Generositatis tuae officioss. M. Johannes Schmidt’ (read on the page image 29 October 2026; the OCR had ‘Praemissum’ and lost the name) — so the leaf records a presentation to a Smil, not to Tycho; who Schmidt and Smil were is not known, and no source reconciles the leaf with Tycho's portrait binding on the volume. Šolc 2018 (pp. 201–202) quotes Falkenstein's lines as ‘ein weiteres Tychonisches Buch in Dresden’; Falkenstein's ‘Daran:’ chain places the Boiemus in the same binding as the Paulus Alexandrinus and the Horoscopographia. Lost with them in 1945 (Norlind 1970, p. 356). Grade B. The SLUB's war-loss register carries a card for the Boiemus — Lit.Graec.B.1976, earlier ‘Phil. gr. B. 93a. Misc. 3’, and ‘Misc. 3’ matches Falkenstein's order, in which the Boiemus is the third piece; no card was found under the other two headings, and the register does not say whether the volume was removed in 1945–46 or destroyed (Nachweiskatalog image 00504111, read 27 October 2026; the identification with the Tycho volume is inference, C).

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 34:2; Norlind 1970, p. 340; the library’s record 14 A 66/adl.1. The title of the Basel edition of 1550 announces Ptolemy’s Liber fructus with Trapezuntius’s commentary as an appendix (‘Adiectus est Cl. Ptolemaei liber Fructus, cum commentariis Georgii Trapezuntii’). open_questions: Whether Kleinschnitzová’s 34:3 (Norlind 1970, p. 358) is the Liber fructus appended to the Bonatus of 1550 or a separately printed Centiloquium bound after it — a question for the volume 14 A 66.

27 Oct 2026 — the Manuscriptorium facsimile holds the Bellanti only (title at canvas 1 to the device leaf at canvas 312, verified 27 October 2026); the Bonatti and anything bound after it are not digitised, so the question remains one for the volume itself (the leaf after Bonatti col. 848 and the final gathering).

entries.subject: Astronomy/Mathematics

marks.annotations: not in the Manuscriptorium facsimile (verified 27 October 2026)

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 12:2, ‘Manuskript … Brahes Autograph’ (Truhlář no. 2761); Norlind 1970, p. 340; the National Library’s early-prints record 14 C 20/adl.1 enters it under the Uraniborg edition of 1591. Twenty quarto leaves in a professional copyist’s hand, the content Tycho’s (Šíma and Valeška 2002; Dreyer, Opera omnia I, p. 315, had already denied the hand), dated ‘Calend. Januar. 1591’, with a distich dated ‘A. C. 1595, 13 Cal. Xbris’ (Prusík 1901). Published in facsimile by Studnička (1886) and by Dreyer (Opera omnia I, pp. 283–293). Bound after the Rheticus Canon of 1551 in the volume 14 C 20, whose title carries the note ‘Vide in fine Dogmata Tychonis Brahe m. p. scripta’. Gingerich and Westman (1988, pp. 24–26) trace the misattribution: Studnička's facsimile of 1886 took the manuscript for Tycho's autograph; Dreyer, in the biography of 1890 (p. 362 n.) and in Opera omnia I, pp. 315–318, found the body not his and the title-page signature doubtful (‘neither the “T,” “B,” nor “h” were typical of Brahe's autograph’), his test the two-stroke M never used by Tycho; Studnička (1901) then argued from this manuscript to the De revolutionibus marginalia, and Horský's facsimile of 1971 rested on the same circle. The two hands are, in their judgement, different from each other and both unlike Tycho's. Tycho names the manuscript to Hagecius on 14 March 1592 as the pamphlet of rules that lay ‘open for teaching in our library on each table’ (Opera omnia VII, p. 325; 1988, p. 62).

marks.annotations: Published as Tycho's autograph by Studnička (1901, 1903) and so listed by Kleinschnitzová (1933); not his hand, and never shown to have been his, according to Dreyer (Opera omnia I, p. 317); a professional writer's hand (Šíma & Valeška 2002); the text excerpted from Proclus's commentary on Euclid I (Basel 1533), interrupted by notes and drawings of sundials (Dreyer, Opera omnia I, p. 317, after Heiberg); the hand excluded as Tycho's by Šíma & Valeška 2002, p. 156
marks.binding: taken out of the Clementinum composite MS XII A 12 (Truhlář: ff. 225–230) between 1901 and 1905–06 and bound alone

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 2; National Library, Clementinum, Sign. XII A 28. Six folio leaves of excerpts from Proclus’s commentary on the first book of Euclid, published by Studnička as Tycho’s autograph (1901, 1903). Dreyer denied that the hand is Tycho’s and found no sign that the manuscript had ever been his (Opera omnia I, p. 317); Norlind (1970, p. 340) reports both views. Status disputed, D, since 20 October 2026: no ownership mark; Dreyer denied hand and ownership (Opera omnia I, p. 317) and Šíma & Valeška give the hand to a professional writer — a contested identification, by the Definitions disputed.
open_questions: Whether the manuscript belongs to the library at all: Kleinschnitzová counts it among the Clementinum Tychoniana as an autograph, while Dreyer found neither Tycho’s hand nor any sign of his ownership (Opera omnia I, p. 317), and no ownership mark is recorded; a comparison of the hand or an ownership mark on the leaves would decide.

norlind.entry: Brahe, Tycho: Brevissimum planimetriæ compendium sua manu exaravit Tycho Brahe. 2°. [Manuskript; papper.] Truhlář nr 2105. Kl. nr 2. – Prag, UB.
norlind.ownership_verdict: located manuscript, Prague; per Dreyer neither written by Tycho nor ever in his possession (contra Kl. and Studnička) – Norlind reports the rejection
norlind.discussion: Den lilla skriften (6 foll.) har ansetts vara en Tycho Brahe-autograf, så bl.a. av Kl. och av Studnička, som utgav den 1903. Men enligt Dreyer (I, 317) är den varken skriven av Tycho eller har den någonsin varit i hans ägo.

entries.title_transcribed: Tychonis Brahe Tabulae sinuum.
entries.subject: Astronomy/Mathematics

marks.inscription: short inscriptions on the end leaves, which Šíma & Valeška (2002) neither prove nor exclude as Tycho's; f. 1r: 'Collegij Caesarei Soc[ieta]tis IESV / Pragae. A.o 1642. / Ex Bibliotheca Tichoniana.' and a Greek line consistent with Prusík's 'οἰστέον καὶ ἐλπιστέον'; f. Iv: 'Numerorum / scientia' in red ink (Manuscriptorium canvases 4, 43, read 27 October 2026)
marks.annotations: the tables are in a professional writer's hand (Šíma & Valeška 2002); published as Tycho's autograph by Studnička (1901)
marks.binding: original binding, T. B. O. 1582 (Norlind 1970, p. 340); front board stamped TABVLAE SINVVM / 1582 (canvas 1); spine later re-covered in marbled material (canvas 3)

entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933 no.1; NK Clementinum Sign. VI E 9. The tables are in a professional writer's hand (Šíma & Valeška 2002); the binding carries Tycho's initials and the year 1582. A third reading of the manuscript's content stands beside Studnička's (Tycho's own, 1901) and Šíma & Valeška's (a professional writer, 2002): the editors of the Prague Mechanica of 1996 call VI E 9 Rheticus's seven-figure tables of 1582, in manuscript, with 1′ increments (Hadravová, Hadrava & Shackelford 1996, p. 162 n. 291) — recorded as their attribution, not adopted; whether the tables are Rheticus's (the Opus palatinum's trigonometric canon was Otho's edition of 1596) is a question for the manuscript itself.

norlind.entry: Brahe, Tycho: Tychonis Brahe Tabulæ sinuum. [Manuskript; pergament.]
norlind.ownership_verdict: located manuscript, Prague; Tycho's autograph copy and adaptation of Copernicus's Canon (original binding with initials T. B. O. 1582)
norlind.discussion: Egenhändig avskrift och bearbetning av Copernicus' »Canon semissium subtensarum rectarum linearum in circulo» 1540. – Truhlář nr 1124. Kl. nr 1. – Prag, UB. Originalbd med initialerna »T. B. O. 1582».

entries.title_transcribed: Carmen epicum de Varadino (manuscript poem)
entries.subject: Poetry

acquisition.channel: sent by the author; the first copy was lost in transit, a second was sent in September 1600 (Opera omnia VIII, 337; VIII, 380)

entries.editorial_note: Brasch sent the manuscript poem, which celebrates Melchior von Roedern’s defence of Grosswardein (Várad) in 1598, to Tycho twice: in August 1600, when it was lost in transit (Opera omnia VIII, 337), and as a replacement in September 1600 that ‘probably reached’ him (Opera omnia VIII, 380; Norlind p. 340); von Roedern died on 20 September 1600. No surviving manuscript codex has been located in any catalogue. Martin Brasch the Younger also published a printed Varadini Hungariae propugnaculi... anni 1598 (1598) on the same subject — plausibly the same matter in print beside an authorial manuscript redaction of 1600, though no source collates the two. The first copy never arrived, the replacement only ‘probably’ did, no codex survives, and no ownership mark that could be looked for attaches to the item; the entry therefore rests on the correspondence alone. Status lost since 20 October 2026: a unique manuscript sent and probably received, not a mass-survival text — the class retired as unlocatable does not fit it.

norlind.entry: Brasch, Martinus: [Carmen epicum de Varadino.]
norlind.ownership_verdict: sent by the author (first copy lost in transit, a second copy sent Sept. 1600 probably reached Tycho)
norlind.discussion: Brasch besjunger här Melchior Rhederus' (von Rödern) segerrika försvar av Grosswardein (Nagy-Várad) mot turkarna. Han skickade dikten till Tycho i aug. 1600 (VIII, 337), men försändelsen kom aldrig fram. Ett nytt exemplar skickade Brasch i sept. s.å. (VIII, 380), vilket förmodligen nådde adressaten.

entries.title_transcribed: Camoeracensis acrotismus seu Rationes articulorum physicorum (Wittenberg, Z. Crato 1588)
entries.subject: Natural philosophy/Polemic

marks.inscription: a dedication to Tycho on the title (the attribution to Bruno's own hand and the date are not secure — see the entry's note of 27 October 2026); on the last page the epigram ‘Nullanus, nullus et nihil, / Conveniunt rebus nomina saepe suis’, given to Tycho’s hand by Šolc (2002, p. 331) and left open by Šíma & Valeška (2002, pp. 158–159: ‘it could be written by Tycho, but it is not certain’); Read on the facsimile 27 October 2026: the dedication at the foot of the title is trimmed and faded — '[…]i nobilitate g[ene]re […] | […] D. Tychoni […] | h[…] […] et […]' (canvas 5); the epigram on the rear free endleaf reads 'Nullanus nullus | est nihil, | Conveniunt rebus nomina | sæpe suis.' (canvas 174)
marks.annotations: ink nota-crosses pp. 9, 15; pointer p. 18; trimmed two-line gloss p. 42 (re-read 27 October 2026); hands unattributed
marks.binding: limp vellum with ties (canvases 1, 176); spine not imaged

entries.editorial_note: Dedication copy sent to Tycho about 1588 (Šolc 2002, p. 331). NK Clementinum, Sign. XV K 22 (olim 8 I 70), catalogued at Chomutov in 1671. The epigram on Bruno’s name on the last page is in a hand that Šolc gives to Tycho and that the handwriting analysis of Šíma and Valeška leaves open; the attribution to Tycho is graded D. How the Acrotismus reached Uraniborg is not settled: Kořán (1969) and Horský (1975) proposed Hagecius as the intermediary; Sturlese (1985, pp. 324–325) objected that only one letter passed between Hagecius and Tycho in 1588 and suggested the carrier of Morsing's Diarium to Bruno (Westman 2011, pp. 304–305 and p. 568 n. 127). In the De immenso (1591) Bruno names Tycho on the comets and on the proper motion of the stars (p. 305). Hedged 27 October 2026 (register dossier §17-06): a dedication to Tycho on the title is secure — three faded, trimmed lines, ‘Omni nobilitatis genere [Kořán: gratiae] insigni et famosis.o illustri et excell.o D. Tichoni Dano in signum benevolentiae et obsequii’ (del Giudice 2008; Šíma & Valeška 2002, p. 158); that it is Bruno's own hand rests on the word ‘author’ Kořán read in 1969, now erased, on Šíma & Valeška's unargued statement and on del Giudice's unpublished comparison; the arrival ‘by 17 August 1588’ rests on ‘Iordanus Nullanus in quodam scripto de Mundo contra Peripateticos’ in a letter known only as printed in 1596 (Opera omnia VI 144–149), and Šíma & Valeška put the gift after 1597 ‘somewhere in Germany’; the carrier is unknown (Westman 2011, p. 304 n. 127). Hand, date and carrier are not secure.

entries.title_transcribed: Sphaera
entries.subject: Cosmological poetry
entries.editorial_note: Norlind (1970, p. 341): from Tycho to Rothmann, January 1587 (Opera omnia VI, 102), Tycho seems to have owned a then recently published edition — Paris 1585 (4°) or rather Herborn 1586 (8°); the Herborn edition of 1587 is too late for the letter. The edition is Norlind’s conjecture, and the ownership rests on one phrase of the letter; no mark attests a copy.

norlind.entry: Buchananus, Georgius: Sphæra.
norlind.ownership_verdict: owned per letter to Rothmann (a then newly issued edition), edition unknown — Lutetiæ 1585 or rather Herbornæ 1586 guessed
norlind.discussion: I denna dikt skildrar Buchanan de enligt hans mening vådliga konsekvenser jordens vridning kring sin axel skulle medföra. — Av Tychos brev till Rothmann jan. 1587 (VI, 102) att döma synes han ha ägt en då »nyss utg.» uppl. av denna dikt. Man skulle kunna gissa på upplagan Lutetiæ 1585 (4°) eller — kanske snarare — Herbornæ 1586 (8°). Upplagan Herbornæ 1587 (8°) passar dock ej med datum för brevet.

entries.title_transcribed: Problema mathematicum
entries.subject: Astronomy/Astrology/Mathematics
entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 6:4: ‘Kein Tychonianum’. Bound at the Clementinum into the composite 5 G 42 with works of other provenance; the volume’s binding is the college’s, and only the Heron (the inscription of 1642) and the Werner (Tycho’s marginalia) are his. Entered so that the work is not claimed for the library from its shelfmark. Printed forty years after Tycho’s death.

entries.title_transcribed: [Nova-1572 tracts] Von dem Cometen ... 1572 + the fuller Erfurt 1573 redaction
entries.subject: Astronomy (nova 1572)
entries.editorial_note: Norlind 1970 (p. 341): ‘Tycho måste ha ägt åtminstone tvenne upplagor av skriften’ — in the Progymnasmata (Opera omnia III, 279–288) Tycho writes that Busch published two German tracts on the new star; one, Norlind reasons, is among the editions Zinner 2574 and 2609–2613 (Augsburg and Erfurt, 1572–73), the fuller one Zinner 2614 (Erfurt 1573, 25 leaves). Busch’s tract on the comet of 1577 has its own entry.

norlind.entry: Busch, Georg: Von dem Cometen, welcher in diesem 1572. Jar ... erschienen. 4°. Z. 2574, 2609–2614.
norlind.ownership_verdict: owned at least two editions (per Progymnasmata); the fuller one must be Z. 2614 Erfurt 1573, the other one of Z. 2574, 2609-13
norlind.discussion: Om den nya stjärnan 1572. Utkom i flera upplagor tryckta i resp. Augsburg och Erfurt 1572–73. Tycho måste ha ägt åtminstone tvenne upplagor av skriften. Vid diskussionen av densamma i »Prog.» (III, 279–288) skriver han nämligen, att Busch om den nya stjärnan publicerat tvenne skrifter på tyska. Den ena kan vara endera Z. 2574, 2609–13 (alla i 4°). Den andra, som Tycho säger vara ännu utförligare, måste vara Z. 2614 Erfurt 1573.4°. Den omfattar 25 blad mot de föregåendes 6–16 blad. — Av Erfurt-upplagan (Z. 2610) utkom en svensk översättning i Stockholm 1573, 12 blad, 4° (Collijn, »Sveriges bibliografi», 2, Sthm 1927–31, s. 427).

entries.title_transcribed: Beschreibung von zugehörigen Eigenschafften … des grossen und erschrecklichen Cometen
entries.subject: Astronomy (comet)
entries.editorial_note: Norlind 1970, p. 341 (Zinner 2764; Hellman 21): listed among the books of the library because Tycho discusses the tract in the comet book (Opera omnia IV, 365–366); no copy, receipt or mark is recorded. Norlind’s introduction states the principle on which such tracts enter his catalogue: it may be regarded as fairly certain that nearly all the writings on the new star of 1572 and the comet of 1577 that Tycho reviews in the Progymnasmata and the comet book stood in the library on Hven (p. 335). An unbound tract of this kind, if Tycho’s copy survives, would carry no known mark by which it could be recognised.

norlind.ownership_verdict: discussed in kometboken only; ownership not stated
norlind.discussion: Diskuteras i kometboken (IV, 365–366).

entries.title_transcribed: Calvini Epistolae & responsa, editio tertia, with Beza's Vita Calvini (Hanau: Wilhelm Antonius 1597, 8°, VD16 C 304) bound with Theocriti Idyllia & Epigrammata, with Moschus, Bion and Simmias, Greek and Latin ([Heidelberg]: Commelinus 1596, 8°, VD16 ZV 14910)
entries.subject: Reformed theology/Greek lyric

marks.inscription: Tycho's dedication on the verso of the front free endpaper facing the Calvin title, read on the leaf 21 October 2026: ‘Johanni Lindenouio | Conſobrino suo | Tycho Brahe | ddt.’ — four lines on one rising diagonal in one ink, the last letter of the name e-shaped where the pen failed at the joint (Mortensen 1955, p. 26) and read o, one long s only, arc u-marks over ‘-ou-’ and ‘suo’, no diaeresis on the y, the display signature about 1.8 times the body, ‘ddt’ after the name under two long strokes with a point after — d(ono) d(edi)t (Fund og Forskning X, 1963, p. 155; Mortensen printed d(onum) d(onavit)); wholly in Tycho's hand, probable (the Graphonomicon specimen copenhagen-kb-calvin-lindenov-dedication, grade B)
marks.annotations: no reader's marks seen in the leaves photographed; the volume's later marks (21 October 2026): the Royal Library's pencils ‘88,-201’, ‘1954 g. 230’, ‘Boghist. Saml.’, ‘BOX’, ‘S-1977’, a cancelled ‘D.A.?.?’, ‘1597’ on the Calvin title and ‘dupl’ on the Theocritus title; a continental ‘fol. 9781’ (the 7 crossed) and ‘36’ on the rear pastedown, the pencil code ‘fij’ at the foot of the Theocritus title, an erased pencil note on the free endpaper, removed labels on both pastedowns, a scraped inscription above the device on the Calvin title; a seventeenth-century ink spine title ‘Johannis Caluini | Epistolae et Respons[a] | Theocriti | Idyllia et Epigra[m]ata’
marks.binding: examined 21 October 2026: gilt parchment over stiff pasteboard, 175 × 120 × 75 mm (leaves 171 × 106 × 70 mm), three sewing supports laced through the covering at the joints, a flat untooled spine with a later ink title, two pairs of green silk ties (remnants in the slits), all edges stained red and plain, plaited natural-thread endbands; on each board a gilt leaf roll with a twisted central line (c. 7–8 mm wide, leaf pitch c. 5 mm, corners overrun) with four five-petalled double roses with hatched barbs, c. 11 mm, in the corners and the oval at centre — the portrait on the front, the arms on the back, both the small die, c. 58 × 42–43 mm on the ruler, the gilt mostly worn; concordant with Mortensen's 5.8 × 4.3 (1955, p. 25), Friis's 59 × 42.5 on the Vienna quartos (1868–69, p. 251) and Strahov Σ VI 3 (58 × 43, 18 September 2026); Mortensen's ‘Spor af grønne Bindebaand’, ‘Rullestempel’, ‘Rosetter’ and the later spine title confirmed; the place of binding undetermined but the tools of the Hven family — the laurel roll of Gigas's Epistolae and GKS 307, a rose punch unlike theirs and unlike Σ VI 3's star but near the Magini rose of Hven — so Wandsbek 1597–98 or Copenhagen 1597 before Prague; the rose punch is not the Hven presentation rose (c. 14.5 mm: Stockholm RAR 106 A, the Dibner and Johan Adolf Epistolae, the Hazmburk Mechanica) nor the Magini rose (9.5–10 mm) but a third punch of 11 mm — a binder with his own tools in the Hven idiom, place open (tested 21 October 2026 at one scale)

entries.editorial_note: A Tycho Sammelband repatriated from the USA (through the ship-broker Hjalmar Bruhn); the only book from his own library at KB besides the autograph observations. Given by Tycho to his cousin Hans Lindenov after the Calvin edition of 1597 had appeared — probably before 1599, Mortensen supposes, unless the book was sent to him later (Mortensen 1955, pp. 26–27). Worn parchment binding, gilt portrait/arms supralibros. Mortensen 1955, pp. 25–27. The recipient is Hans Christoffersen Lindenov til Ørslevkloster (d. by 7 April 1610), lensmand at Bergenhus 1578–86 — the officer to whom the crown's four letters on Tycho's Nordfjord fief were addressed — and lastly at Hammershus 1594–1610; he was on Hven for one night, 3–5 July 1594 (the diary, pp. 218–219). Tycho's consobrinus in the strict sense: Mortensen corrected Danmarks Adels Aarbog 1902, which lists Hans under Christoffer Lindenov's second wife Ide Rantzau, to the first marriage with Margrethe Clausdatter Bille (b. 1525), Beate Bille's sister; DAA dates neither marriage, and the correction stands unrefuted (Mortensen 1955, p. 27; DAA 1902, pp. 286–287; DAA 1890, p. 87). The Calvin edition stood in the Frankfurt Lent-fair catalogue of 1597 under ‘Libri Calvinianorum’ (Lutz, A2v): Tycho, who in 1574 had called Calvin's tract against the astrologers learned and its author over-strict (TBOO I, pp. 170–172), and who praised Beza in the Progymnasmata (TBOO II, p. 325), acquired the Reformed letter-book in the months after his own Epistolarum astronomicarum liber and in the spring his Hven pastor was convicted for failing to admonish him (22 April 1597). The Royal Library's acquisition falls between January 1952 and the article of 1955; the copy to be examined on 21 October 2026 is 88, 201 01801 (eks. 2), the first copy being Scavenius's of 1665. A pre-visit dossier of 21 October 2026 prepared the examination. Examined in the Royal Library on 21 October 2026: the volume is eks. 2, 88, 201 01801, acquired in 1954 (the accession pencil ‘1954 g. 230’); the dedication read on the leaf and the hand assessed (wholly Tycho's, probable; the son excluded on context, a secretary at the same desk not excluded by the photographs); the dies measured and the binding described; the Theocritus is VD16 ZV 14910 with the Commelinus ‘Veritas’ device (ΑΛΗΘΕΙΑ ΠΑΝΔΑΜΑΤΩΡ), the Calvin VD16 C 304 with Antonius's later device, the pelican on the mountain; Kancelliets Brevbøger keep Hans Lindenov on Bornholm in 1597–1602, so the gift was handed over in Copenhagen in the spring of 1597 if at all in person, or sent.
open_questions: Collate both constituents (Calvin [28] Bl., 804[=806] pp. and a final blank; Theocritus [8] Bl., 319, 30 pp., [1] Bl., 150 pp. in three parts) and record whether Scaliger's Emendationes and Casaubon's Theocriticarum lectionum libellus are bound in; the leaves photographed on 21 October 2026 were the titles, the end of the Calvin index and the dedication opening.

Whether the dedication's first two lines are Tycho's or a secretary's at his desk (see the volume's open questions): Jessenius disfavoured on his VI F 44 entry of 8 January 1599; Longomontanus and Tengnagel untested.

entries.title_transcribed: In hoc libro haec insunt: Hippocomicus, quae est disputatio de curandis equis. Xenophontis liber de re equestri Latinus factus. Nomina equestria Graeca & Latina. Xenophontis libri de repub. Lacedaemoniorum & Atheniensium. Itemque de praefectura equestri, conversi in sermonem Latinum. Historia rei nummariae, sive de nomismatis Graecis & Latinis
entries.subject: Letters/Philosophy

marks.inscription: Vedel's name ‘Andreas Seuerinus Velleius’ at the head of the title; the work number ‘1.’ beside it (the later librarian's, matching the contents note on the front flyleaf)
marks.annotations: a red-brown subject heading at the head of sig. A2 recto (‘Dignitas equestris ordinis’ [?]), underlining in the same ink of the Greek style-terms in the preface (sig. A3 verso) and on p. 97, and pen strokes against a passage on p. 141 — otherwise unannotated

dispersal.detail: Vedel’s name stands at the head of the title. Walde (1920, p. 329) and Mortensen (1955, p. 27) read the volume as Tycho’s gift to Vedel, the memento of their Leipzig years; Norlind (1970, p. 366) held it more likely that the book was Vedel’s from the start, given to Tycho, who had it bound with the two others — on which reading it did not leave the library in his lifetime and its route to De la Gardie is undocumented.

entries.editorial_note: Prandtl Verzeichnis A no. 58 (‘Xenophon in lateinischer Übersetzung. Wittenberg, 1556’); bound first in Band III. The title page shows the work to be Joachim Camerarius's Hippocomicus with his Latin Xenophon, printed at Leipzig by Valentin Papst in 1556 ([24], 342 pp.), as Norlind 1970, p. 366, already had it under Xenophon; Prandtl's and Mortensen's ‘Wittenberg’ is a slip. Corrected from the facsimile, 12 October 2026.

norlind.entry: Xenophon: In hoc libro insunt. Hippocomicus quæ est disputatio de curandis equis ... Lipsiæ 1556. 8°. Pr. nr 58. — UUB.
norlind.ownership_verdict: located copy, Uppsala; Norlind holds the volume Vedel's, given to Tycho and bound by him, against Walde's reading of it as Tycho's gift to Vedel
norlind.discussion: Pr. nr 58. — UUB. Inleder ett saml.-bd med Osius och Garcæus. Originalbd. På pärmen »Ty Brad 1563». Volymen har enligt Walde (»Storhetstidens litterära krigsbyten», 2, Upps. 1920, s. 329) troligen skänkts av Tycho till Vedel, vars namnteckning finns på titelbladet. Sannolikare synes det mig emellertid, att skriften från början tillhört Vedel, som skänkt den till Tycho, vilken i sin tur låtit inbinda den och de båda andra i ett enda band.

entries.title_transcribed: Bohemais, hoc est De ducibus Bohemicis libri duo; De regibus Bohemicis libri quinque
entries.subject: History and antiquities
entries.editorial_note: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 32:2; Norlind 1970, p. 341; the library’s record 9 B 135/adl.1 reads the two parts as one imprint — Šolc 2002 (p. 331) itemised the De regibus separately; it is a part of the one imprint and has no entry of its own. Bound after Alma’s Bellum giganteum in the white parchment binding with Tycho’s gilt portrait and arms, catalogued at Chomutov in 1672. Šolc (2006, printed p. 193 (scan 7)) connects the Candidus with Prague and the Bohemian setting — Tycho and his Protestant family ‘hoped for a lasting settlement in Bohemia’ — a reading of why the books were there, not a mark in the book.

entries.title_transcribed: Ephemerides ad annos XIX (1557-1575)
entries.subject: Ephemerides/Tables
entries.editorial_note: Norlind (1970, p. 342), citing Dreyer, states that Tycho ‘skaffade sig under sin Leipzigvistelse’ this edition — acquired it during his Leipzig years — and cites it often in his earliest observation journal (Opera omnia X, 5 ff.). Dreyer’s sentence is narrower: ‘In his observations from 1563–64 he also mentions the Ephemerides of Carellus (Venice, 1557)’ (Tycho Brahe, Edinburgh 1890, p. 18, n. 1); the acquisition at Leipzig is Norlind’s inference. The edition is Venice: Vincenzo Valgrisi, 1557, 4to; its title runs ‘ad annos XIX’, 1557 to 1575, where Norlind prints ‘IX’. Three datings stand side by side: Šolc 2006 (printed p. 190 (scan 4)) places the Carelli ephemerides for 1557 with the Stadius among the tables Tycho ‘procured at once’ after the eclipse of 21 August 1560, unsourced; Norlind's Leipzig purchase is an inference from Dreyer p. 18 n. 1 (the citations in the observations of 1563–64); and the loci record of the Copenhagen years (after Christianson 2020, pp. 19–22) has the Carelli bought with Jens Nilsson in Copenhagen about 1561. Šolc's 1560 is not adopted. Westman (2011, p. 240) writes that Tycho, like Hagecius, ‘owned and annotated’ a copy of Carelli's Ephemerides; his note (p. 557 n. 80) cites the edition only, and no copy is named.

norlind.entry: Carellus, Johannes Baptista: Ephemerides ... ad annos IX, incipientes ab anno Christi 1557 usque ad annum 1575 ... Venetiis 1557.4°.
norlind.ownership_verdict: owned — acquired by Tycho during his Leipzig years (after Dreyer) and often cited in his earliest observation journal; no copy located
norlind.discussion: Enligt Dreyer (»Tycho Brahe», s. 18¹) är det denna upplaga som Tycho skaffade sig under sin Leipzigvistelse och ofta nämner i sin tidigaste observationsjournal (X, 5 ff.).

entries.title_transcribed: Astrolabium
entries.subject: Astronomy/Instruments
entries.editorial_note: Norlind 1970, p. 342: a letter to Rantzau of February 1597 (Opera omnia VII, 381) shows Tycho owning at least four works by Clavius, one of them since identified among his books in Prague (the Apologia of 1588, Kleinschnitzová 13:2); the Astrolabium he cites to Herwart in November 1599 in a way that presupposes ownership, criticising Clavius for praising, in its Lemma III, Ursus’s method of solving spherical triangles from the Fundamentum astronomicum (Opera omnia VIII, 201). A common quarto; a copy of Tycho’s would carry no known mark by which it could be recognised.

norlind.ownership_verdict: presumably owned (cited to Herwart, Nov. 1599, in a way that presupposes ownership); not located
norlind.discussion: [Unheaded prefatory paragraph, printed before this headword and introducing the Clavius entries:] Av ett brev till Rantzau febr. 1597 (VII, 381) synes framgå, att Tycho ägde åtminstone fyra verk av den berömde jesuiten Clavius; ett av dessa har i själva verket identifierats bland hans böcker i UB., Prag. [Entry proper:] I ett brev till Herwart (nov. 1599; VIII, 201) citerar Tycho detta verk på ett sådant sätt, att man väl måste förutsätta, att han ägt det. Han kritiserar nämligen Clavius för att denne i »Lemma III» i boken lovordar hans antagonist Ursus' metod (i »Fundamentum astronomicum») att lösa sfäriska trianglar.

entries.title_transcribed: Gnomonice (Gnomonices libri octo)
entries.subject: Gnomonics/Sundials

acquisition.channel: bought for Tycho by Heinrich Brucaeus at Rostock, March 1586, valued at seven Joachimsthaler (Opera omnia VII, 100)

entries.editorial_note: Brucaeus bought Tycho a copy of Clavius’s Gnomonices at Rostock in March 1586 (his letter of 15 March 1586: ‘emi et tibi Gnomonicen CLAVIJ Bambergensis’, valued at seven Joachimsthaler; Opera omnia VII, 100). The purchase was conditional: the bookseller had deposited the books with Brucaeus at the beginning of the winter and would take them back if Tycho did not want them or already had them (‘Emi autem hac conditione, ut si tibi forte non placerent, aut forte eosdem iam esses nactus, Bibliopola ad se recipiat … Iam enim libros ineunte hyeme apud me deposuit’, VII, 100); whether this copy reached Hven is not recorded (Norlind 1926, p. 214, no. 3). That Tycho had the work is his own statement to Rantzau of 22 February 1597: Clavius’s writings on Euclid, on Sacrobosco and on gnomonics ‘in promptu habeo, et iamdudum introspexi’ (VII, 381). In December 1584 the Rostock bookseller, back from Frankfurt without the books Tycho had ordered, had sold his one copy, valued at nearly five Joachimsthaler, to Heinrich Rantzau (Opera omnia VII, 88; Norlind 1926, p. 214, no. 3), so Tycho’s first order went unfilled.

acquisition.channel: gift/exchange

entries.editorial_note: Cort Aslakssøn sent the commentary to Tycho in 1594 (Aslaksson to Tycho, 23 October 1594: ‘CLAVIJ hunc in Sphæram SACROBOSCI Commentarium ad te ablegavi ob tractatulum quendam de Nova Stella’), and Tycho received it. Tycho himself names it among the works of Clavius he has to hand, writing to Rantzau on 22 February 1597 (Opera omnia VII, 381: ‘ea nihilominus quae in Euclidem ingeniose et in Iohannem de Sacrobusco luculenter, et de Gnomonicis copiose conscripsit, in promptu habeo, et iamdudum introspexi’). No copy with Tycho’s marks has been identified: the one work of Clavius among the Clementinum volumes is the Apologia of 1588, bound after Maestlin’s Alterum examen (Kleinschnitzová 13:2, Sign. 14 G 30), not this commentary. Grade set on 20 October 2026 under the document rule (a surviving copy with his marks, or a document naming the book as his, is A; a dedication, the 1642 note alone or a queried mark is B; a third party's report or the compiler's inference is C).
