sources.label: Zeeberg 1993
sources.full: Peter Zeeberg, *Den praktiske muse: Tycho Brahes brug af latindigtningen* (Studier fra Sprog- og Oldtidsforskning 321; Copenhagen: Museum Tusculanum, 1993); pp. 14–17 on the first prints of the Uraniborg press, the poem to Erik Lange of 27 November 1584 and the dating of the poems.
sources.role: The first item printed on the Uraniborg press, from Tycho's own observation protocol.

sources.label: Rauch 1914
sources.full: Christian Rauch, ‘Zu den Wappen Peter Apians’, *Zeitschrift für Bücherfreunde*, N.F. 5 (1913/14), pp. 223–224, with one illustration. On information from the Gotha Oberbibliothekar Rudolf Ehwald: describes the Gotha *Astronomicum Caesareum*, its arms apparatus and Tycho's inscription, which it prints in full, and states that the book came to Gotha from Munich. Norlind's ‘Chr. Rausch’ is a misprint.
sources.role: The first publication of the Gotha inscription.

sources.label: Gingerich 1971
sources.full: Owen Gingerich, ‘Apianus's Astronomicum Caesareum and its Leipzig Facsimile’, *Journal for the History of Astronomy* 2 (1971), pp. 168–177. The Gotha copy was taken apart for the facsimile (p. 169); the facsimile's penultimate leaf reproduces ‘a handsome autograph inscription written in what is now the Gotha copy by Tycho Brahe on 14 June 1599’ (p. 172).
sources.role: The facsimile's source copy and the inscription, from the scholar who handled the dismantled volume.
sources.url_label: ADS — the scanned article as a PDF

sources.label: Schaffner catalogue 1977
sources.full: *The Joseph Halle Schaffner Collection in the History of Science: a selection exhibited at the Joseph Regenstein Library of the University of Chicago, October 1977 – January 1978* (Chicago: University of Chicago Library, 1977). Preface by Sidney F. Huttner, essay by Jacob Zeitlin, catalogue by Richard Meier, provenance research by Edith Brinkel; 107 entries. Entry 15, the Apianus: ‘German half calf; dated 1686 … Silver 4. Presented by Tycho Brahe … to his pupil Paul Wittich, October 29, 1580’; the foreword explains the ‘Silver’ numbers as lots of the Newberry Library's sale of Silver duplicates at Sotheby's, 8–9 November 1965, and Zeitlin names Warren Howell as Schaffner's buyer at that sale.
sources.role: The holding library's own statement of the presentation, the binding and the Silver provenance.

sources.label: Newberry, Movable Mayhem
sources.full: Newberry Library, Digital Collections for the Classroom, ‘Movable Mayhem: Pop-Up Books through the Ages’: ‘This copy, owned by Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe and given to his student, is now at the University of Chicago … It was also briefly at the Newberry, when the library acquired Louis Silver's collection in 1964. Yet it was never accessioned, and was sold to help defray the costs of the Silver sale.’ With an image of the Chicago copy, credited to the University of Chicago.
sources.role: The Newberry's own statement of the 1964 purchase and the 1965 sale.

sources.label: Chicago, Schaffner exhibit
sources.full: University of Chicago Library, online exhibit ‘Joseph Halle Schaffner Collection in the History of Science’: ‘the copy of Apianus's Astronomicum caesareum (1540) was presented by Tycho Brahe to his pupil, Paul Wittich, October 29, 1580’.
sources.role: The holding library's online statement of the presentation.

sources.label: Mortensen 1942
sources.full: Harald Mortensen, ‘Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag’, *Astronomiska Sällskapet Tycho Brahe, Årsbok 1942*, offprint pp. 13–27. Pp. 23–25 on the library: the Clementinum's 97 books and manuscripts in 47 volumes and the volumes outside Prague (p. 23), the Uppsala Sammelband after Walde (*Storhetstidens litterära krigsbyten*, II, 1920, p. 329), the volume of 1561 sold from Munich to America (the firm printed as ‘Wells & Co.’, for Weiss & Co.), the count of 110 works in 57 volumes and the estimate of about 5,000 volumes; pp. 14–15 the Lipsius note of 5 April 1592 in Høst's Danish rendering.
sources.role: The intermediate count of 1942 and the estimate of about 5,000 later withdrawn; the date and text of the lost Lipsius note.

sources.label: Roos 1948
sources.full: Carl Roos, ‘Om nogle vaaben- og portrætprydede danske bogbind fra slutningen af det 16. aarhundrede’, *Bogvennen*, ny række 3 (1948), pp. 134–152, with figs 1–29 on pp. 153–177; the Tycho bindings pp. 143–144 and fig. 26.
sources.role: The one binding-historical placement of the portrait and arms plaques: after the model of the Frederik II portrait-plate bindings, oval where such plates are rectangular, ‘mere italiensk-franske end tyske’ in style.

sources.label: Bogvennen 1966
sources.full: ‘Noter juni 1966’ (signed E. D.), *Bogvennen* 1966, pp. 200–207: the sale of Oscar and Lia Ekman's library (Bruun Rasmussen auction 186, 1–4 November 1965) — the volume from Tycho's library withdrawn as a bequest to Kronborg, Rundetaarn's unsuccessful bid on ‘en lignende hos Sotheby’, the *De nova stella* of 1573 at 71,000 kr. and a *Mechanica* of 1602 at 17,000 kr.
sources.role: The volume of 1561 still the museum's in 1965; the Sotheby's lead.

pages.loc: pp. 200–207, the passage on the Tycho volume
pages.via: tidsskrift.dk; the viewer opens on scan page 6, where the withdrawn Tycho volume and the Kronborg bequest are reported (scan pages 6–8).

sources.label: Magasin 1987
sources.full: ‘Kronik’, *Magasin fra Det Kongelige Bibliotek* 2:1 (1987), pp. 25–42, at pp. 31–33: the Sammelband of 1561 deposited by the Handels- og Søfartsmuseet in the Royal Library's Håndskriftafdeling, the contact arranged by Claus Thykier of Ole Rømers Museum; the notes in several hands, the Leipzig matriculation list of 16 October 1561 and the herbarium suggestion.
sources.role: The earliest witness to the deposit of the volume of 1561 at the Royal Library.

pages.via: tidsskrift.dk; the viewer opens on p. 31 (scan page 7), the deposit of the Sammelband of 1561.

sources.label: Fund og Forskning 1963
sources.full: ‘Tilføjelser og rettelser til Fund og Forskning 1954–62’, *Fund og Forskning i Det kongelige Biblioteks Samlinger* 10 (1963), pp. 152–162, at p. 155, on Mortensen 1955: ‘I dechiffreringen under autografen side 26 bør forkortelsen ddt opløses til dono dedit eller dedicavit.’
sources.role: The correction of the Lindenov dedication's abbreviation.

sources.label: Fund og Forskning 1965
sources.full: ‘Efterslæt til tidligere årgange’, *Fund og Forskning i Det kongelige Biblioteks Samlinger* 12 (1965), p. 156, on Brøndsted 1962, after W. Norlind: Tycho's description of Ptolemy's appearance is taken from the preface of the Latin *Almagest* printed at Venice in 1515, which he owned and names in a letter (*Opera omnia* VI 95); the elegy itself stands in the *Epistolae* (*Opera omnia* VI 269).
sources.role: Norlind's identification of the Venetian *Almagest* as the edition of 1515, and the use Tycho made of it.

sources.label: Hlinovský & Pišna 2018
sources.full: Jiří Hlinovský & Jan Pišna, *Vzal jsem tu knihu z rukou anděla / I took this book from the hands of an angel: Výstava duchovních exlibris ze sbírky Strahovské knihovny, 28. 8. – 30. 9. 2018* (Praha: Strahovská knihovna, 2018), pp. 6–15 — the library's own bilingual history of its ownership marks: Hirnheim's library rule of 1672 (point 8: every book to be inscribed to the monastery on its title leaf), the eighteenth-century collections of Jan Josef Klauser, Šebestián Heidel and Antonín Strnad and their marks (Klauser's printed ex-libris; Strnad's handwritten name and name-stamp), and the five stamps the library used from the late eighteenth century to the early twentieth (the large 38 mm BIBLIOTHECAE STRAHOVIENSIS stamp of the late eighteenth century, the 26 mm reduced stamp, the oval, the round 30 mm stamp with the late-gothic shield, and the small STRAHOV stamps of 1909).
sources.role: The marks by which a Strahov accession is dated and its stratum recognised.

sources.label: Hyklová 2017
sources.full: Petra Hyklová, ‘Dědictví klementinských exaktních věd a druhý život „Matematického muzea“ v 19. a 20. století’, *Acta Universitatis Carolinae – Historia Universitatis Carolinae Pragensis* 57/2 (2017), pp. 45–62 (DOI 10.14712/23365730.2018.49). The Clementinum's Mathematical Museum (1722–1785) and its historians; Seydl's study of Strnad's library, which identified two hands in Strnad's own book-list and matched it against the Strahov volume catalogue (p. 49); Strnad's inventory of the Museum of 1781, reprinted in Czech translation from Seydl 1951 as an appendix (pp. 53–57).
sources.role: How Seydl established which Strahov books came from Strnad — the method behind the cataloguer's doubt about the Regiomontanus.

sources.label: Voit 2021
sources.full: Petr Voit, ‘Role knižní vazby při revitalizaci Strahovské knihovny za opata Jana Lohela’, *Bibliotheca Strahoviensis* 14 (2021), pp. 115–126. The Prague binderies of the 1580s–1610s in the Strahov holdings: the Master with the Eagle (at least 40 volumes) and the ‘Knihvazač rudolfínského okruhu II’ (about 70 volumes), the latter's work reaching Strahov by several routes — Pontanus's gifts of 1595, the sixteen books of the imperial councillor Franz Gottfried Troilo von Lessoth, Pavel Pistorius z Lucka — and not only by purchase (p. 118); the second version of Lohel's supralibros lent only to this binder in 1605–1615 (p. 119); the title inscription ‘Liber Monast: B. V. M. Montis Syon vulgo Strahow 1608’ (p. 119, n. 23).
sources.role: The binder of the *Opus palatinum* in his Strahov context; the dated parallel for the *Mechanica*'s title inscription.

sources.label: Novotný 2021
sources.full: Jan Novotný, review of Petr Voit, *Vzácné knižní vazby Strahovské knihovny v Praze: od gotiky na práh baroka* (Praha 2020), *Acta Musei Nationalis Pragae – Historia litterarum* 66 (2021), no. 1–2, pp. 96–98 (DOI 10.37520/amnpsc.2021.009): the monograph treats ‘the group of presentation copies bound for the astronomer Tycho Brahe, which share one decorative concept — a gilt frame, a dominant lozenge, the portrait supralibros on the front board and the armorial on the back’.
sources.role: What Voit 2020 contains, from a reader of it; the monograph itself is print-only.

sources.label: Voit 2023
sources.full: Petr Voit, *Boj o volnou plochu* (Praha 2023), pp. 209 and 560 — cited by the Strahov catalogue record of the *Opus palatinum* (Σ V 5/a) beside Voit 2020, pp. 250–252. Not read.
sources.role: A second published treatment of the *Opus palatinum* binding, as the holding library cites it.

sources.label: PROVENIO — Kraus z Krausenbergu
sources.full: Knihovna Národního muzea, PROVENIO provenance authority kpw3257450, ‘Kraus z Krausenbergu, Daniel, 1579–1637’ (rejected form ‘Crusius a Krausenberga’): born at Jirkov in the Chomutov district, studied at Altdorf in 1599, Bohemian incolat with his father Martin in 1606, physician at Königsberg in Bavaria, a book-owner traced in three Bohemian collections; ‘Měl dva syny Gabriela a Jana Václava’ — he had two sons, Gabriel and Jan Václav (consulted 19 September 2026).
sources.role: The one documentary lead to who Gabriel Crusius was — a lead, not an identification.

sources.label: Prusík 1901
sources.full: Bořivoj Prusík, ‘Tychoniana der Prager k. k. Universitäts-Bibliothek’, *Mitteilungen des Österreichischen Vereins für Bibliothekswesen* 5 (1901), Nr. 4 (23 November 1901), pp. 197–201. The first printed list of the Clementinum Tychoniana, made during the recataloguing begun in 1898: four manuscripts (the Praxis appended to 14 C 20; the Tabulae sinuum of 1582, MS VI E IX, in brown leather with ‘T. B. O.’; the mathematical fragment MS XII A XII; the Sacrobosco compendium MS VII E XXIX, formerly bound in 14 F 16) and sixteen printed works in four groups by binding — plain (14 A 59, 1 H 56, 14 F 16, 14 J 164, 14 J 192, 14 B 16, 5 B 70, 5 C 31), brown leather with ‘T. B. O.’ (14 H 190, 14 H 225, 14 J 190, 14 K 70), and the Prachtbände in white (14 J 176, 14 G 30) and brown leather (8 H 39, 12 H 10). Prusík held that Tycho bound his books more richly as his means grew, the conjecture Kukula repeated and Bargum answered.
sources.role: The 1901 list behind Kukula and Kleinschnitzová; the earliest shelfmarks of twenty Clementinum records.

sources.label: Mitteilungen 1901 (notice)
sources.full: ‘(Die Prager Bibliotheken und Tycho Brahe.)’, Vermischte Nachrichten, *Mitteilungen des Österreichischen Vereins für Bibliothekswesen* 5 (1901), Nr. 1 (29 January 1901), pp. 51–52. The tercentenary notice: Studnička's *Prager Tychoniana* and the planned exhibition of all Prague Tychoniana; the son's album of 1598, long in the Klebelsberg family and bequeathed by Count Franz Klebelsberg to the Bohemian Museum; the Triangulorum praxis and the sine tables in the University Library; Plan's album at Strahov; six printed works from Tycho's library; the two sextants of the observatory.
sources.role: The announcement of the 1901 recataloguing finds and the Klebelsberg provenance of the son's album.

sources.label: Kukula 1906–07
sources.full: Richard Kukula, ‘Die Tychoniana der Prager K. K. Universitäts-Bibliothek’, *Zeitschrift für Bücherfreunde* 10 (1906/07), Heft 1, pp. 17–25, with four facsimiles (the entry in the son's album, the entry in Plan's album, the price list in the Sacrobosco manuscript, the Praxis). The director of the University Library on the state of the Tychoniana after the recataloguing: Prusík's four manuscripts and sixteen works (twenty-eight with the bound-in pieces), and since 1902 twenty-two further works in seven volumes — XVI J 38, V J 103, V G 92 and V J 2 stamped ‘T. B. O. 1576’, XIV F 8 and XIV A 63 with the initials ‘T. B.’, and XIV J 199 with Kepler's two tracts of 1606 — five manuscripts and fifty printed works in twenty-eight volumes in all; the custos Truhlář's discovery of the Sacrobosco manuscript and its price list, which led back to the Sammelband marked ‘constat 5 15’; the Mansfeld Reinhold, the Archimedes volume, the Ptolemy and the Copernicus (whose glosses he still gave to Tycho). His conjecture that the rich bindings belong to Tycho's last years was answered by Bargum in the same volume.
sources.role: The 1906 count (5 manuscripts, 50 works, 28 volumes) and the first publication of seven Clementinum volumes.

sources.label: ZfB 1906–07 (binding note)
sources.full: ‘Ein Bucheinband Tycho Brahes’, *Zeitschrift für Bücherfreunde* 10 (1906/07), Heft 1, Chronik, pp. 42–43, with three facsimile plates of the two supralibros (signed ‘—W—’ in the contents). The Munich antiquarian bookseller Ludwig Rosenthal had sent the volume: the eighteenth volume of Zwinger's *Theatrum humanae vitae* (Basel 1587) in wooden boards covered in brown leather, two chased brass clasps, seven raised bands, three blind-tooled frames, the innermost with fourteen portrait medallions of scholars, four gilt rosettes, and the gilt portrait and arms medallions with their distichs; a manuscript note inside the board called it a ‘Schweizer Ledereinband mit Blinddruck und Goldmedaillons’, and the writer supposed it made at Basel for Tycho. The volume is the one now at the Röhsska museum, Göteborg.
sources.role: The 1906 description and the Rosenthal step in the provenance of the Röhsska volume.

sources.label: Bargum 1906–07
sources.full: G. Bargum, ‘Über Tycho Brahes Buchdruck und Bucheinbände’, *Zeitschrift für Bücherfreunde* 10 (1906/07), Beiblatt (Chronik), pp. 124–126, signed ‘Kopenhagen. G. Bargum’. A reply to the binding note of Heft 1 and to Kukula: the Uraniborg press was at work by 1584, not 1596; the plaques served as the mark of Tycho's library and as his printer's and publisher's device; Hasselberg's three binding types; the German library copies of the *Mechanica*; the Zwinger volume ‘kein schweizer, sondern ebenfalls ein dänischer, unter Tychos persönlicher Anleitung hergestellter’ binding, though the fourteen medallions have no parallel on his other bindings — Tycho was not at Basel in 1587, and Gellius Sascerides, who set out in the summer of 1588, may have procured the book at Basel or at the Frankfurt fair; Kukula's conjecture of late luxury bindings answered with the Ramus and Maestlin–Clavius volumes; and the suggestion that Tycho took from Zwinger's title the name of his projected *Theatrum astronomicum*.
sources.role: The first argument that the Röhsska binding is Danish work, and the *Theatrum astronomicum* remark.

sources.label: Norlind 1926
sources.full: Wilhelm Norlind, ‘Ex bibliotheca Tychoniana. Några anteckningar’, *Nordisk tidskrift för bok- och biblioteksväsen* 13 (1926), pp. 211–218. The first reconstruction from the letters: thirty-two numbered works — Craig's unprinted *Capnuraniae restinctio* among them — that the statements of Tycho and his correspondents place in his hands during the Hven years, and, separately, four loans from other libraries; the library in the round south tower over the laboratory, the ‘musaeum’; no catalogue known, the registration of 21 March 1597 read as a first cataloguing on the eve of departure; the library ‘ett universal-bibliotek’. Written at the prompting of Collijn's systematic search in Prague.
sources.role: The 1926 list that opened the attested tier; the basis of Bilaga I of 1970.

sources.label: Walde 1938
sources.full: Otto Walde, ‘Några böcker från Tycho Brahes krets’, *Nordisk tidskrift för bok- och biblioteksväsen* 25 (1938), pp. 11–17. The Braunsberg find: in the library of the Staatliche Akademie at Braunsberg a copy of Scaliger's *De emendatione temporum* in the revised Leiden edition of 1598, bound in white parchment with Tycho's arms on the lower and his portrait on the upper board, both blind-stamped, with the decor usual on his bindings; not bound on Hven, perhaps at Wandsbeck in 1598; many marginalia in several hands, photographs of which Hans Ræder judged not Tycho's; no dedication; the later note ‘M. Braunhardt i Gotha 1761 … Ex bibliotheca Oppeliana’. Also the Uppsala volume of 1563 given to Vedel and the Glareanus Vedel bought in 1564, now in Prague; the 2781 spine number and its uncertainty; and the books of Johannes Eriksen Hamburgensis, Tycho's amanuensis, which went into Queen Christina's library with the Prague booty (a Pitiscus bought at Prague on 14 August 1601, now at Hanover; two chemical manuscripts at Leiden; a Lull of 1593 at Västerås) — and, apart from them, the Vienna *Commentariolus* manuscript, Longomontanus's gift to Eriksen at Benátky on 18 July 1600, whose supposed passage to Tycho and with his papers to Vienna Walde doubted.
sources.role: The identity of the Braunsberg volume and the Eriksen provenance of the Vienna *Commentariolus*.

sources.label: Hanslik 1851
sources.full: Joseph Adolf Hanslik, *Geschichte und Beschreibung der Prager Universitätsbibliothek* (Prague 1851), p. 274 (the Copernicus of 1566, B 16, with ‘die zahlreichen von Tycho Brahe's eigner Hand an den Rand geschriebenen Bemerkungen’ — the library’s own description giving the glosses to Tycho), p. 556 (Tycho's printed works, XLIX B 59–60) and p. 612 (the Dogmata geometrica appended to XIV C 20, brought to light by the custos Dambeck, and the parchment Tabulae astronomicae et canones XIV A 18, which Ungar had given out as Tycho's autograph and Hanslik, from the form of the numerals, placed far earlier). Cited by Friis 1868–69.
sources.role: The earliest published attribution of the Copernicus glosses and the Praxis to Tycho; a rejected Tychonianum.

sources.label: Danske Magazin 1746
sources.full: ‘Endnu videre Følge af rare og mest utrykte Efterretninger om Tyge Brahe’, *Danske Magazin*, 1. række, II (Copenhagen 1746), 23. Hefte, pp. 321–322, with an engraving of the portrait stamp at the head. The earliest printed description of the two supralibros: the portrait stamp Tycho ‘selv ladet … i et Stempel udgrave, og brugt samme til at lade i Guld aftrykke uden paa Bindet af sine Skrifter’, seen on the *Mechanica* of 1598 in blue satin that he gave on 18 December 1600 ‘til en fornemme Herre i Bømen’, then at the Royal Library; the three chains, Frederick II's portrait with the letters F. S., the elephant; the arms stamp of the same form and size with its verses.
sources.role: The first printed notice of the ownership stamps.

sources.label: Kepler, GW XIX (1975)
sources.full: Johannes Kepler, *Gesammelte Werke*, XIX: *Dokumente zu Leben und Werk*, ed. Martha List (Munich: C. H. Beck, 1975), section 5, ‘Rudolphinische Tafeln’, Nr. 7: Kepler to Georg Brahe, Vienna, 16 November 1624 (Vienna, Österreichische Nationalbibliothek, Cod. 9737, fol. 29, autograph), pp. 202–203. Answering Georg Brahe's letter of 15 October, Kepler proposes that the heirs have ‘einen vleissigen Catalogum’ written of all that remains of Tycho's library in books and manuscripts, asks them to look after the woodblocks and copperplates of the *Mechanica* and the engraved portrait, and wants in particular ‘Hipparchum de fixis graecè, ist ein klains folium, vnd vil drinnen manu Scaligerj’. The same section prints the Kepler–Tengnagel contract of 8 July 1604 (Nr. 1–2, pp. 189–190) and the heirs' dealings with the imperial commissioners in the 1620s. The volume is available at the Bavarian Academy.
sources.role: The library remnant still in the heirs' hands in November 1624, and the Scaliger Hipparchus among it.

sources.label: Jardine et al. 2005
sources.full: Nicholas Jardine, Dieter Launert, Alain Segonds, Adam Mosley and Karin Tybjerg, ‘Tycho v. Ursus: The Build-up to a Trial, Part 1’, *Journal for the History of Astronomy* 36 (2005), pp. 81–106, at pp. 96–103. The copy of Ursus's *De astronomicis hypothesibus* (Prague 1597) that Tycho lent to Holger Rosenkrantz in 1598, with the offending passages marked, and did not recover: the Royal Library's copy from the Rosenkrantz sale of 1695 carries no marks; the copy in the Danish National Library of Science and Medicine, 4° Astr. 8050 — perhaps transferred from the Royal Library in 1918–26 — is inscribed ‘Donum Autoris’ and carries sixteen clear marginal marks, all against passages insulting to Tycho, chiefly in the dedication to Landgrave Moritz and the invective poem; the authors argue that it is the copy prepared for Lange and lent to Rosenkrantz.
sources.role: A candidate for the Ursus volume Tycho lent and lost in 1598, now in Copenhagen.

sources.label: Fabian, Handbuch (Prague)
sources.full: Vlasta Faltysová (the period after 1945 with Kateřina Hekrdlová), ‘Nationalbibliothek der Tschechischen Republik’, in Bernhard Fabian (ed.), *Handbuch deutscher historischer Buchbestände in Europa, Bd 1.1: Tschechische Republik, Prag, Teil 1*, bearb. Vlasta Faltysová and Pavel Pohlei (Hildesheim: Olms-Weidmann, 1999), the online edition of 2003: §1.13 (among the Clementinum's acquisitions after 1622 ‘wertvolle Autographen des dänischen Astronomen Tycho Brahe (s. u. 2.527 ff.), die von seinen Erben 1642 gekauft wurden’), §1.31 (the Bibliotheca mathematica, kept in Stepling's rooms until 1778, 155 volumes so far identified, after Tobolka 1959, ‘die ältesten und wertvollsten Teile … Autographen des dänischen Astronomen Tycho Brahe’). The online text omits §§2.469–2.537, among them Martin Šolc's section ‘Bibliotheca Tychoniana’ (printed pp. 149–151).
sources.role: The library's entry in Fabian's *Handbuch*, written by its staff: purchase from the heirs in 1642, stated without a reference, against Šolc's donation.

sources.label: Boldan & Kazanskii 2023
sources.full: Kamil Boldan and Andrei Kazanskii, ‘Možnosti využití videospektrálního komparátoru VSC 8000 při studiu znečitelněných vlastnických poznámek v inkunábulích Národní knihovny České republiky’, *Knihovna: knihovnická revue* 34 (2023), no. 2, pp. 22–35, at p. 28 and fig. 5. Among six incunables whose defaced ownership notes were read with the video spectral comparator: the Sammelband 44 F 38 — d'Ailly's *Imago mundi* (Louvain, c. 1477–83) with the Ratdolt Euclid of 1482 — ‘Majitelem konvolutu byl do své smrti 1601 Tycho Brahe’, his ownership shown by the autograph monogram ‘T. B.’ on the manuscript-supplied title leaf and by his glosses; the Chomutov college's note of 1645; the binding year 1576 stamped into the front board; the Kulm brethren's note on the Euclid. The authors note that Kleinschnitzová 1933 does not list the volume.
sources.role: The first publication of a Tycho volume among the National Library’s incunables.

sources.label: Císařová Smítková, Paličková & Vackářová 2021
sources.full: Alena Císařová Smítková, Tereza Paličková and Jana Vackářová, ‘Jezuitské fondy Národní knihovny ČR ve světle provenienčního průzkumu’, *Acta Musei Nationalis Pragae – Historia litterarum* 66 (2021), no. 1–2, pp. 27–43, at p. 30 (DOI 10.37520/amnpsc.2021.003). The National Library's provenance survey of the Jesuit college libraries: 215 volumes with Chomutov inscriptions, seven given before 1600; the college's unusual holding of mathematics and astronomy; ‘minimálně čtyři knihy z pozůstalosti Tychona Brahe’, all with the initial supralibros ‘TBO 1576’ on the front board and a Chomutov note on the title; the authors connect the scientific bent with P. Jan Jüngling (1705–1775), keeper of the Clementinum's mathematical library in 1749 and prefect at Chomutov in 1765–66, and suppose the books were Clementinum duplicates.
sources.role: The library's count of the Chomutov Tychoniana and its (conjectural) explanation of how they got there.

sources.label: Volf 1932
sources.full: Josef Volf, ‘Tycho Brahe a jeho hvězdářská pozůstalost’, *Říše hvězd* 13 (1932), no. 1, pp. 1–9, and no. 2, pp. 21–29 (with a German summary); first printed in *Český bibliofil* (1931), not seen. From the Bohemian chamber records: the instruments and the manuscript observations bought for Rudolf's collections, ‘kdežto knihovna zbyla dědicům’; the 4,000 thaler of September 1603; the rescript of 9 July 1609; the heirs assigned from 1623 to the arrears of the towns Žatec, Kadaň, Rakovník and Chomutov, with payments until 1654; the heirs turned Catholic, and ‘putuje část slavné bibliotéky Brahovy s nádhernými vazbami a se supralibros do klementinské knihovny jako dar’; Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel, captain of the Malá Strana from 1642, gave his share of the debt to the Dominicans of St Giles (Ferdinand III's assurance of 14 March 1643 for 22,534 fl.), Sophie Brahe hers (9,942 fl.) to the Kadaň Franciscans; iron instead of money in 1672; debts still claimed in 1685 and 1688; the Czechoslovak restitution claims of the 1920s against Vienna, with the documents. Read on the page 27 October 2026: part 2, p. 23, the four towns with their sums and dates — Žatec (1,000 thaler), Kadaň (1,000), Rakovník (950), Chomutov (950), ‘ze starých berních nedoplatků (Chomutov, 26. září 1623, Kadaň, 3. července 1626 a j.)’, the instalments running to 1654; p. 24, Ferdinand II's order of 10 November 1631 to pay part of the interest, stopped by the Saxon invasion, and the assecuration of 14 March 1643 to the Dominicans of St Giles for 22,534 fl. 22 kr. 4 d. (Arch. min. vnitra, Bekennen u. Verträge 1642/65); p. 25, Sophie Brahe's 9,942 fl. to the Kadaň Franciscans and the iron of 30 July 1672.
sources.role: The Czech archival account of the estate; the Clementinum transfer called a gift.

sources.label: Dvorský 1883
sources.full: František Dvorský, ‘Nové zprávy o Tychonu Brahovi a jeho rodině’, *Časopis Musea království Českého* 57 (1883), pp. 60–77. The archival report on the heirs: the sale of the instruments and ‘knihy’ to Rudolf II for 20,000 thaler and the rescript of 9 July 1609 that the purchased instruments and books stay in Bohemia. The source behind Dreyer's appendix, Kleinschnitzová's estate pages and Volf. Read on the page 27 October 2026 (pp. 66–77, the Kramerius OCR): the Benátky building accounts of 1599 (pp. 66–68); the petition for citizenship of 1601 and 1603, never decided (p. 69); the sale of ‘the astronomical instruments and books’ for 20,000 thaler, the Fürst–Rebeník assignment of 10 January 1603, the 4,000 of 23–25 September 1603 and the 1,000 of 1604 (pp. 70–71); the rescript of 9 July 1609 and Matthias's bond of 23 April 1614 for 15,000 kop for ‘instrumenta astronomická a knihy … při konci léta 1601 koupené’ (pp. 71–72); the towns' assignments in kopy, Chomutov's letter of 25 February 1623, the heirs' emigration (‘Kam se uchýlili, nevíme’), Jørgen's half-yearly walks to Rakovník and Chomutov, his death in 1640, Sophie's conversion, the family notes (pp. 73–76 and nn. 10–14); the cessions of 1642 — Sophie's 15,000 fl. to Kadaň, Tengnagel's 17,500 fl. to St Giles — and the Těchlovice report of 10 February 1652 (p. 77). No estate inventory and no list of the library is cited anywhere in the article.
sources.role: The archival base of the estate narrative.

sources.label: Hasner 1872
sources.full: Joseph von Hasner, *Tycho Brahe und J. Kepler in Prag. Eine Studie* (Prague: Calve, 1872), 47 pp.; pp. 10–12 on the purchase of the astronomical Nachlass for 20,000 thaler, the half paid by 1608, the rescript of 1609 that ‘Instrumente und Bücher’ stay in Bohemia, and the instruments' passage to the Jesuits of the Ferdinandean university and their later auction.
sources.role: The earliest Prague monograph on the estate.

sources.label: Uppsala UB 2026 — catalogue, photographs, EOD facsimile
sources.full: Uppsala University Library, Specialsamlingar, Script. Graeci (Xenophon). (1) The catalogue records of the three constituents (Alma/Primo; LIBRIS fxqdp8qr4fzxfx8, n9q4jrzml9cl7xd5, 9x1fsp9b7s52412b), the Uppsala holdings revised on 11 September 2026: ‘Ljust garvat skinnband med rikliga blindtryck och spår av spännen. På främre pärmen tryckt: TY BRAD’; ‘På titelsidan handskrivet: Andreas Seuerinus Welleius; Magnus Gabriel De la Gardies röda sigill på främre pärmens insida’; ‘På eftersättsbladet ett handskrivet index’; Garcaeus: ‘Strödda marginalanteckningar’; and the LIBRIS custodial-history note on all three: ‘På främre pärmen tryckt: "TY BRAD 1563"; på titelsidan handskrivet: "Andreas Seuerinus Welleius" ; Magnus Gabiel De la Gardies röda sigill på främre pärmens insida’. (2) Three photographs of the upper board taken by Peter Sjökvist, Rare Books Librarian, in October 2026 with the light raking across the band beneath the Annunciation panel — the remains of stamped forms, a looped figure at the band's right end, the rest abraded, no legible numeral — unpublished, kept with the edition's working papers; and the librarian's confirmation, with the book in hand, that the year 1563 is plainly legible to the naked eye. (3) The digital facsimile of the three constituents made through eBooks on Demand and delivered in October 2026: 371 + 103 + 215 images at about 200 ppi, text block only (the boards are not reproduced); publication in Alvin expected.
sources.role: The holding library's own record of the volume: the catalogue notes and the custodial history, the photographs of the board and the librarian's reading of the year, and the leaf-by-leaf facsimile — Vedel's name on the first title, the work numbers 1–3, the marginalia of the Garcaeus.

sources.label: Uppsala UB, Alvin record 805325
sources.full: Uppsala University Library, Alvin record 805325, 'Sammelband (Script. Graeci [Xenophon], Pp:398)' (urn:nbn:se:alvin:portal:record-805325): former owners De la Gardie, Magnus Gabriel; Brahe, Tycho; Vedel, Anders Sørensen; binding 'Ljust garvat skinnband med rikliga blindtryck och defekta spännen'; fifteen photographs of the binding, pastedowns, endleaves and edges published 12 October 2026 (published October 2026); the EOD facsimile is to be attached to the same record.
sources.role: The holding library's photographs of the binding, the seal, the contents note and the handwritten index; its naming of Tycho as former owner.

sources.label: Museet for Søfart 2026
sources.full: M/S Museet for Søfart, Helsingør: communication of Thorbjørn Thaarup, curator (history and geography), October 2026. The volume 1957:0030 — the student binding of 1561 with Regiomontanus's *Tabulae directionum* (1550) and Apianus's *Cosmographia* (1553) — is part of the museum's collection and is kept at the museum; the deposit at the Royal Library's manuscript department reported in 1987 and 1992 has therefore ended, the date of its return not stated. On the sheet 1954:0495 (the *Danske Magazin* 1746 plate of the Týn epitaph, catalogued ‘Bernigeroth sc.’) the museum has no better photograph at hand and will photograph the foot of the sheet when the curator is next at the archive. Unpublished; a copy is kept with the edition's working papers.
sources.role: The holding museum's own statement of where the volume of 1561 is kept.

sources.label: Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, copy record (K10plus)
sources.full: Forschungsbibliothek Gotha, copy record of Apianus, *Astronomicum Caesareum* (Ingolstadt 1540), Math gr2° 00038/02, in the K10plus union catalogue (PPN 567768368), revised 2024. It transcribes Tycho’s inscription of 14 June 1599, names Duke Friedrich Wilhelm I of Saxe-Weimar as the copy’s recipient and Tycho as donor, and records the copy’s later custody: the catalogue of Duke Friedrich III’s private library; the stamp of the Herzogliche Bibliothek Gotha; the stamp and initial of Duke Ernst II.
sources.role: The holding library’s own record of the Gotha Apianus: the recipient of Tycho’s gift and the volume’s custody to the present.

sources.label: University of Chicago Library, catalogue record 146807
sources.full: University of Chicago Library, catalogue record of Apianus, *Astronomicum Caesareum* (Ingolstadt 1540), Special Collections, alc ff QB41.A639 1540 (VuFind record 146807). Names Tycho Brahe as inscriber and Paul Wittich, Louis H. Silver and Joseph Halle Schaffner as former owners; transcribes Tycho’s presentation inscription of 29 October 1580; describes the binding dated 1686, Silver’s book label and Schaffner’s bookplate.
sources.role: The holding library’s own record of the Chicago Apianus: the gift to Wittich and the volume’s custody from Silver to the library.

sources.label: Biblioteka Kórnicka (WBC)
sources.full: PAN Biblioteka Kórnicka, sygn. Cim.Qu.2812: Reinhold Heidenstein, *De bello Moscovitico quod Stephanus rex Poloniae gessit commentariorum libri VI* (Basel: Waldkirch, 1588), the library’s record and digitisation in the Wielkopolska Biblioteka Cyfrowa (publication 518174, edition 467724; record: ‘supereksl., plak., portret z napisem w otoku’, the arms plate ‘Arma, genus fundi pereunt …’; Estreicher XVIII, 80). The scan was read for this edition on 18 October 2026.
sources.role: The copy itself, the first located volume of the library in Poland; its binding, title and pastedowns read in the scan.

sources.label: Walde 1920
sources.full: Otto Walde, *Storhetstidens litterära krigsbyten: en kulturhistorisk-bibliografisk studie*, II (Uppsala, 1920), p. 329: the first report of the Uppsala volume of 1563 (Prandtl’s Band III) with Vedel’s name on the first title. Cited here after Mortensen 1942 (p. 25) and Mortensen 1955 (p. 27, n. 4).
sources.role: The first report of the Uppsala volume of 1563.

sources.label: Voit 2015
sources.full: Petr Voit, *Katalog prvotisků Strahovské knihovny v Praze* (*Bibliotheca Strahoviensis*, Series monographica 6; Praha: Královská kanonie premonstrátů na Strahově, 2015), nos. R-13 and R-14 — the Strahov Regiomontanus volume DR VII 19, as cited by Boldan 2025 (entries 33.c and 36.a). Not read.
sources.role: The incunable catalogue’s description of DR VII 19; the numbers R-13 and R-14 are taken from Boldan 2025.

sources.label: Jihočeská vědecká knihovna — Klauser
sources.full: Jihočeská vědecká knihovna v Českých Budějovicích, authority file of personal and family names, record m0077300, ‘Klauser, Jan Josef, 1705–1771’ (variant headings Clauser, Johann Josef Klauser): born in Prague on 20 March 1705, died there on 31 July 1771; gubernial archivist, collector, founder and member of the Prague printers’ confraternity, and printer in Prague from 1761 to 1771, first as factor of the archiepiscopal press and then on his own account.
sources.role: The dates of birth and death of Jan Josef Klauser, the Strahov collector through whose library the Euclid AV II 2 reached the monastery.
sources.url_label: Jihočeská vědecká knihovna — authority record m0077300

sources.label: Christianson 1967
sources.full: John Robert Christianson, ‘Tycho Brahe at the University of Copenhagen, 1559–1562’, *Isis* 58:2 (1967), pp. 198–203.
sources.role: The student bindings read against the Copenhagen curriculum; p. 201 n. 13 on the Ptolemy of 1551 (Pratensis as owner, Tycho's probable inheritance in 1576) and the note in Dreyer's hand, Royal Library NKS 3077 4°, p. 101, recording Friis's opinion that the marginalia are Pratensis's.

sources.label: Jardine & Segonds 2008
sources.full: Nicholas Jardine and Alain-Philippe Segonds, *La guerre des astronomes. La querelle au sujet de l'origine du système géo-héliocentrique à la fin du XVIe siècle*, vol. I: Introduction (Paris: Les Belles Lettres, 2008; Science et humanisme 9). The dossier of the Tycho–Ursus quarrel: the depositions of 1598, the suit of 1599–1600, the Copenhagen marked copy restated, Tycho's placing of the library, the Ziegler annotations.
sources.role: The quarrel with Ursus read against the library: the witnesses to its shelves and its room, the Ziegler annotations, the Copenhagen copy, the papers.

sources.label: Veselá 2025
sources.full: Lenka Veselá, *Švédská knižní kořist z českých zemí* (Dolní Břežany: Scriptorium, 2025). The Swedish book plunder from the Bohemian lands, 1631–1648, and where the books are now: the Prague chapter pp. 129–160, the Tycho paragraph p. 142, the transport pp. 201–205, the Stockholm recataloguing pp. 208–214, the Rantzau library pp. 9–10 and 180–183, the holdings census pp. 271–282. Read on the page 27 October 2026: pp. 27–29, ‘Chomutov 1631’ — the Saxon confiscation of the Chomutov college library, the soldiers' sale (Schmidl 1754, p. 119), the buying-back of 1632, the Swedish occupations of 1639, 1645 and 1647.
sources.role: The Swedish road (III) given its dates and limits; the two Tycho manuscripts and the print of Rudolf II's collection; the 1636 Castle catalogue as Ferdinand III's; the Rantzau library's road into the same National Library.

sources.label: Seydl 1951
sources.full: Otto Seydl, ‘Dějiny jesuitského „musea matematického“ v koleji sv. Klimenta na Starém městě v Praze’, *Věstník Královské české společnosti nauk*, třída matematicko-přírodovědecká, 1951, no. VII, pp. 1–59 (English summary pp. 39–40; Antonín Strnad's inventory of 5 August 1781 in Latin pp. 45–51 and in Czech pp. 51–58).
sources.role: The Clementinum's Mathematical Museum from the Jesuit annals to the National Technical Museum — its formal foundation of 1722, its keepers, the portrait prints handed to the library in 1781 and the ‘some books’ still in Strnad's list, the dissolution of 1785: the institution whose library held the Tychoniana from 1642.

sources.label: Mačák 1995/96
sources.full: Karel Mačák, ‘Ke vzniku matematického muzea v Klementinu’, with the German version ‘Zur Entstehung des mathematischen Museums im Klementinum’, *Miscellanea oddělení rukopisů a starých tisků* 12 (1995/96), pp. 74–78.
sources.role: The inscription of 1638 on NK 14 E 3 and Vydra's Kresa passage: a Musaeum mathematicum existed at the Clementinum before the Tycho books arrived, and the foundation of 1722 crowned nearly a century of growth. The copy read lacks the issue's plate with the photograph of the inscription.

sources.label: Šolc 2006
sources.full: Martin Šolc, ‘Knihovna Tychona Brahe’, in Vlasta Faltysová (ed.), *Rukověť tištěných knihovních fondů Národní knihovny České republiky od prvotisků do konce 19. století* (Praha: Národní knihovna ČR, 2006), pp. 189–193.
sources.role: The Czech account of the Bibliotheca Tychoniana by the library's own specialist: the 1642 transfer as a donation of the unsaleable astronomical remainder, the Vitellio–Dürer volume ‘probably by sale’ in 1636, the counts of 1898, 1933 and since, the printed concordance of Kleinschnitzová's numbers with the shelfmarks. The citation rule of p. 189: the Clementinum volumes are cited by Kleinschnitzová's Soupis 1–47, a new find is expressly flagged as belonging to the Bibliotheca Tychoniana, and an unnumbered title ‘either did not survive or is kept elsewhere than in the Clementinum’; the p. 189 count (more than 110 prints and 5 manuscripts in 52 volumes) repeats 1999, § 2.527; also the places-of-printing and subject profile (p. 193), the edge-wear evidence of use (p. 191), Ungar's departments of the 1780s and the four gift volumes (p. 192), and the statement that the Clementinum's copies of *De nova stella*, *De mundi* and the *Mechanica* are not Tycho's (p. 190).

sources.label: Šolc 1999
sources.full: Martin Šolc, ‘Bibliotheca Tychoniana’ (§§ 2.527–2.537), in Bernhard Fabian (ed.), *Handbuch deutscher historischer Buchbestände in Europa, Bd 1.1: Tschechische Republik, Prag, Teil 1*, bearb. Vlasta Faltysová and Pavel Pohlei (Hildesheim: Olms-Weidmann, 1999), pp. 149–151 — the chapter the online Fabian edition omits.
sources.role: The German account of 1999: more than 110 prints and 5 manuscripts in 52 volumes; the heirs left with the library to sell; the Sammelband ‘presumably’ bought in 1636; the books recorded in a catalogue in 1642. Not to be cited for persons and titles without checking: on p. 150 Šolc calls the copy Hájek gave Tycho at Regensburg in 1575 ‘eine Abschrift des Comentariolus von Georg Joachim Rhaeticus’ (the work is Copernicus's), makes Paul Wittich ‘aus Kassel’ (he was of Wrocław) and Longomontanus ‘aus Kopenhagen’ (a Jutland peasant's son who studied there), and lists Willem J. Blaeu among the pupils and co-workers who lived in the Curtius house (Blaeu wintered on Hven in 1595–96 and is not recorded in Prague); on p. 151 he prints the Copernicus of 1566 as ‘libri IV’ (for VI). His Czech text of 2006 repeats the first three, so they are his settled wording, not misprints.

sources.label: Riegger 1795
sources.full: Joseph Anton von Riegger, *Archiv der Geschichte und Statistik, insbesondere von Böhmen*, Dritter und lezter Theil (Dresden: Waltherische Hofbuchhandlung, 1795), pp. 214–230: ‘Catalogus seu consignatio librorum, qui in bibliotheca serenissimi et potentissimi regis Bohemiae in arce Pragensi reperiuntur anno 1636’, printed from a contemporary manuscript sold in 1782.
sources.role: The one catalogue of the Castle library, read on the page on 19 October 2026 (MDZ bsb10008769, scans 252–268): eleven sections, 368 entries, no Tycho, Kepler or Copernicus title; Ferdinand III's own name and school exercise books among the entries, Rudolf II once as dedicatee; the Rožmberk library's four-volume catalogue already on the Castle shelves (p. 229).

sources.label: Švédská knižní kořist (database)
sources.full: Švédská knižní kořist z českých zemí 1646–1648 [online databáze], Knihovna Akademie věd ČR (Lenka Veselá and others), catalogue at https://krigsbyte.lib.cas.cz/ — 4,367 records of identified booty books in 63 libraries (state of October 2026; about a quarter not yet examined in hand).
sources.role: Searched in full on 19 October 2026 for Tycho: three imprints (DK 963, RK 943, RK 621), no Tycho-owned book, no Tengnagel, no Brahe in the 79-record Prague-Castle group — the test of channel III's hopes.

sources.label: Balsem 2020
sources.full: Astrid C. Balsem, *Een biografie van de Bibliotheca Vossiana* (doctoral thesis, Leiden University, 2020), with catalogues of Vossius's medical, philosophical and mathematical books.
sources.role: What of Vossius's Stockholm spoils touched the Tycho orbit: the 1666 quadrant ‘formerly presented by Tycho Brahe to the Emperor Rudolf’, the Leiden Ursus *Fundamentum* with a Prague provenance of 1595, the *De nova stella* 1371 D 10, Hermann Bulder's astronomical library, the Rožmberk and Ferdinand III books among the Vossiani; no Tycho manuscript in the catalogued rubrics.

sources.label: Jankovics & Monok 1993
sources.full: József Jankovics & István Monok, *Dudith András könyvtára. Részleges rekonstrukció / András Dudith's Library. A partial reconstruction* (Szeged: Scriptum, 1993; Adattár XVI–XVIII. századi szellemi mozgalmaink történetéhez 12/3), 207 pp.; English introduction pp. 9–16; the catalogue of traced books with Dudith's D-numbers; Appendix 2, Bussow's *Catalogus Bibliothecae Nicolsburgensis*. With the 1994 summary (*Magyar Könyvszemle* 110) and Monok's addenda of 2025.
sources.role: The reconstruction of the library Tycho tried to buy in 1600: about 4,000 volumes by the D-numbers on the head edges, under ten per cent traced; the roads Dietrichstein–Christina, Dresden and Hartenfels. No. 44 is Tycho's gift of the *De mundi* to Dudith (Stockholm, KB RAR 106 A).

sources.label: Mainx 1940
sources.full: Felix Mainx, ‘Die Bücherei des Prämonstratenser-Stiftes in Prag’, *Sankt Wiborada: ein Jahrbuch für Bücherfreunde* 7 (Augsburg 1940), pp. 41–43 — journal, volume, place and year supplied by identification; the leaves print only the title and the by-line ‘Von Dr. Felix Mainx’.
sources.role: A bibliophile's three-page notice on the Strahov library written three years before Mainx reported the eight supralibros volumes to Mortensen: it names no supralibros volume and no marginal note, gives Strahov's original editions of Copernicus, Tycho Brahe and Kepler as ‘from the possession of the Prague astronomer A. Strnad’, and names two Stammbücher with entries of Melanchthon and of Brahe (printed p. 43) — the 1940 witness to the Strnad stratum and the negative for the Mainx-8.

sources.label: Antonín 1994
sources.full: Luboš Antonín, ‘Alchymie a přírodověda v rukopisech a starých tiscích zámecké knihovny Valdštejnů v Mnichově Hradišti’, *Zprávy památkové péče* 54 (1994), no. 6, pp. 183–186 (German summary p. 186).
sources.role: The Waldstein castle library at Mnichovo Hradiště — the Duchcov library founded by Jan Bedřich z Valdštejna, at Duchcov until 1921 — its size, its strata and its finding aids; names no Tycho volume. The *De nova stella* Collijn placed there is a census matter.

sources.label: Vackářová 2026
sources.full: Jana Vackářová, *Století proměn astronomie. Od Koperníka k Brahemu a Keplerovi* (Praha: Národní knihovna ČR, 2026; Z klementinských pokladů, sv. 4), 54 pp. — the National Library's curator on the Clementinum copy of *De revolutionibus* (14 B 16) and the Prague Tychoniana; no footnotes; select bibliography p. 48; list of illustrations with shelfmarks pp. 49–53.
sources.role: The binding of 14 B 16 described and photographed (the pictorial panels; a binding apart from Tycho's); the Copernicus year 1973 and Horský's facsimile of 1971 (BMMS Facs F 158); how Gingerich came to join the Vatican and Prague copies; the Clementinum copy's lack of the fol. 82 note; the 2026 photographs of the two binding types (14 J 176, 14 J 190); Hájek's recommendation of Wittich (after Smolka) and the names she gives among those Tycho asked to secure Wittich's books.

sources.label: Collijn 1933 (as Kleinschnitzová printed it)
sources.full: Isak Collijn's report to Flora Kleinschnitzová of two Tychoniana outside Prague — a Paulus Alexandrinus (Wittenberg 1588) in Tychonic original binding in the Landesbibliothek Dresden, and a *De nova stella* (1573) in the Waldstein library at Mnichovo Hradiště — printed by Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 78 n. 1 (‘Einer freundlichen Mitteilung Dr. I. Collijns zufolge …’). The report itself, a letter, is not held; it is known only as she printed it.
sources.role: The witness behind the Dresden Paulus Alexandrinus and the Mnichovo Hradiště *De nova stella* — second-hand, through Kleinschnitzová.

sources.label: Ilsøe 1999
sources.full: Harald Ilsøe, *Det kongelige Bibliotek i støbeskeen. Studier og samlinger til bestandens historie indtil ca. 1780*, 2 vols (Danish Humanist Texts and Studies 21; Copenhagen 1999).
sources.role: The provenance history of the Royal Library's early holdings — where the Lindenov Calvin–Theocritus, the Fincke and Flemløse volumes and the Prague booty of 1648 in Copenhagen are to be traced; the registers are the way in. The reading against the Royal Library volumes is still to be made.

sources.label: University of Texas Libraries, catalogue record
sources.full: University of Texas Libraries, catalogue record of the Harry Ransom Center's copy of Gesner, *De omni rerum fossilium genere* (Zurich 1565), Alma 991019307189706011 (fetched 9 September 2026): the only Gesner 1565 *De omni rerum fossilium genere* at the Ransom Center; the record's local note reads ‘Wilhelm Prandtl Collection’, the provenance Gingerich 2002 gives for this volume.
sources.role: The holding library's record of the Texas volume (Prandtl's Band XXI), as the chapter registers catalogue records for Gotha, Strahov and Uppsala.

sources.label: Hadravová, Hadrava & Shackelford 1996
sources.full: Alena Hadravová, Petr Hadrava and Jole Shackelford (eds), *Tycho Brahe: Instruments of the Renewed Astronomy* (Prague: KLP, 1996) — the commented edition of the *Mechanica*; the Bibliotheca Tychoniana at p. 162 n. 291.
sources.role: The 1996 editors' reading of VI E 9 as Rheticus's seven-figure tables of 1582 in manuscript — a third attribution of the Tabulae sinuum, recorded on e-kl-1.

sources.label: Maggs 582 (1933)
sources.full: Maggs Bros., *Catalogue 582: Medicine, Magic and Natural Sciences* (London, 1933), item 155, p. 92, £125 — ‘Volume from the Library of Tycho Brahe … with Notes in his Hand’: Regiomontanus, *Tabulae directionum* (Tübingen, Morhart, 1550) bound with Apianus–Gemma, *Cosmographia* (Paris, Gaultherot, 1553); ‘Tycho Brade’ on the front cover, ‘Anno 1561’ on the back; the half-torn fly-leaf with ‘Sum Tychonis Brade / Epts thaliro & 4 Gross’; the Helsingborg longitude-and-latitude note; ‘See Prof. Prandtl's Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe, 1933, which describes and illustrates our volume.’ The entry is not illustrated (plate XI, facing p. 92, is Rossell's Verdadero conocimiento de la peste, item 291).
sources.role: The first dealer's offer of Band II after Weiss & Co.: London, not America, in 1933.
sources.url_label: Wellcome Library copy at the Internet Archive (leaf 106 = p. 92)

pages.via: Wellcome Library copy at the Internet Archive, leaf 106, opened on the page with ‘Brade’ highlighted.

sources.label: Maggs 600 (1934)
sources.full: Maggs Bros., *Catalogue 600: Fine Books, Manuscripts and Engravings* (London, 1934), item 260, p. 208, £125 — the same volume re-offered: ‘“Tycho Brade” stamped on front cover, and “Anno 1561” stamped on back cover’, the fly-leaf ‘(torn)’, Prandtl 1933 cited for ‘our volume’.
sources.role: Band II still unsold in London in 1934.

sources.label: Maggs 666 (1938)
sources.full: Maggs Bros., *Catalogue 666: A Catalogue of Books in Foreign Languages of All Periods, including Greek Papyri and Oriental and European Manuscripts* (London, 1938; 176 pp.), item 451, p. 166, £125 — the same volume, under the heading ‘From the Library of Tycho Brahe’, the entry reprinting Catalogue 600's text word for word: Regiomontanus, *Tabulae directionum*, Tübingen, Morhard, 1550, bound with Apianus, *Cosmographia*, Paris, Gaultherot, 1553 (1551 at end), ‘2 vols. in 1, 4to, contemporary binding of stamped brown leather, with “Tycho Brade” stamped on front cover, and “Anno 1561” stamped on back cover’; inside the front cover and on the fly-leaf ‘(torn)’ the notes by Tycho including ‘Sum Tychonis Brade Epts thaliro & 4 Gross’; Tycho ‘only 15’; the marginal note giving the longitude and latitude of Helsingborg; ‘See Prof. Prandt's Die Bibliothek des Tycho Brahe, 1933, which describes and illustrates our volume.’ Item 452 on the same page is the 1602 *Mechanica* from the Radcliffe Observatory, Oxford (£28). Read at HathiTrust (full view, uc1.$b199380, sequence 174), where a second copy of the catalogue is held search-only (uc1.$b706956).
sources.role: Band II still with Maggs in 1938, five years after its first offer, at the unchanged £125.

pages.via: HathiTrust, full view, sequence 174 (the Berkeley copy catalogued under the catalogue's title; the copy catalogued as ‘Catalogue no. 666’, uc1.$b706956, is search-only).

sources.label: Reichner, Catalogue 1 ([1939])
sources.full: Herbert Reichner, *Catalogue 1: Rare books, manuscripts, prints, maps* (New York, [1939]; 110 items, 64 pp.; a copy pencilled ‘Fall, 1940’), item 72 — ‘a book from Tycho Brahe's library’ (Robin Halwas's description of the run of Reichner's stock catalogues, after Dickinson 1998, pp. 172–173). Search-only at HathiTrust: the entry runs over two pages matching Morhard, directionum, Regiomontani, Tubingen, 1550, Gaultherot, Brade, 1561, 1553, Apianus, *Cosmographia*, Helsingborg, Groschen, binding, stamped, student, Leipzig, Copenhagen, Prague; ‘Prandtl’ and ‘Philobiblon’ match no page; the only round price sharing the Brade page is 850, so $850 is the probable asking price (an inference; item 73 begins on the same page). Not in Reichner's Catalogues 2–9 (1940–48). Reichner (1899–1971) had published *Philobiblon* and Prandtl's Sonderdruck in Vienna, left on 13 March 1938 and opened in New York in 1939–40.
sources.role: The volume's arrival in America, about 1939–40, and the last printed witness before the Ekmans.

pages.loc: the catalogue record (search-only; ‘Brade’ matches one page)
pages.via: HathiTrust holds this catalogue search-only. Its search-inside page returns a blank page to the public (October 2026: the server answers that access is denied and the viewer draws nothing), so the link opens the catalogue record, which confirms the holding and its limited view. The page tests were read from the search page's underlying data on 20 October 2026 (item 72 runs over two pages).

sources.label: Royal Library, Håndskriftafdelingen, Aktuelt (November 2001)
sources.full: Det Kongelige Bibliotek, Håndskriftafdelingen, ‘Aktuelt’, November 2001 (the department's web newsletter; Wayback copy of 5 November 2010): under ‘Udstillinger’, the department lent to the Ole Rømer Museum's exhibition ‘Tycho Brahes mange ansigter’ (25 October – 31 December 2001) ‘Tycho Brahes eksemplar af Johannes de Monte Regio, Tabulae Directionum, 1550 (Acc. 1986/116, depositum fra Handels- og Søfartsmuseet)’.
sources.role: Dates the Royal Library deposit to 1986 (Acc. 1986/116) and shows the volume still on deposit at the end of 2001.

pages.via: The Royal Library's Wayback copy of the department's newsletter page.

sources.label: Kraks Blå Bog 1937
sources.full: *Kraks Blaa Bog* 1937, p. 276, s.v. ‘EKMAN Oskar Ingeniør’: born 13 October 1885 in Copenhagen, son of the steam-miller Oskar Ekman (d. 1898) and Ida Burmeister (d. 1936); married 28 December 1915 Lia, born 10 December 1894 in Hamburg, daughter of the wholesaler Emil Pouplier and Mathilde Brincker; cand. polyt. 1910; joint owner of Nordisk Elektricitets Selskab from March 1913, sole owner from September 1913; Søndermarksvej 13, Valby. The register volume 1910–1988, p. 32, gives his death as 16 September 1956.
sources.role: The donors' identities and dates; the correction of ‘founder of NES 1908’.

pages.via: Project Runeberg: the page of Kraks Blaa Bog 1937, facsimile and OCR text.

sources.label: New York Times Book Review, 28 May 1933
sources.full: Philip Brooks, ‘Notes on Rare Books’, *New York Times Book Review*, 28 May 1933: a review of Maggs Catalogue 582 that singles out ‘a remarkable volume from the library of Tycho Brahe’ in Maggs's words.
sources.role: How the volume became known in America in 1933 while still in London — possibly all that lies behind Prandtl's ‘nach Amerika verkauft’.

pages.via: Internet Archive lending copy of the issue: borrow it, then search ‘Tycho’ to reach the column ‘Notes on Rare Books’.

sources.label: Thykier 2003
sources.full: Claus Thykier, ‘Rapport vedrørende undersøgelse af: Joannis de Monte Regio … Tabulæ directionum profectionumque’, Ole Rømer Museet, 13 January 2003 — an unpublished one-leaf typescript report on the volume of 1561 (Band II), which he examined at the Handels- og Søfartsmuseet's library in 1985 and had deposited at the Royal Library's manuscript department in 1986 (acc. 1986/116). It records the gift (January 1957, from civilingeniør Oskar Ekman; further provenance unknown), the stamps TVCHO BRADE and ANNO 1561, the spine number 204 (‘formodentlig katalognummeret i Tychos eller et senere bibliotek’), the forperm's inscriptions as he reads them — ‘Tyge Brahe’ struck through, ‘tico brahe ven’ struck through (‘en lidt barnlig skrift’), in another hand ‘Sum Paul…’ with the rest lost on the torn-off part, the price ‘… 4 taliro & 4 Gross.’ under a struck line where ‘Brade’ can be glimpsed — short astronomical notes in Tycho's hand inside the binding, on the forperm's back and in the margin of the preface's tenth page, and the herbarium: Latin plant names at the head of 36 unpaginated pages in a hand other than Tycho's, plant remains in the gutter of 26 of them identified by Jette Baagøe and re-housed in envelopes, one plant name unattested before c. 1623 (Peter Wagner and Baagøe), hence a user who ‘formentlig ikke har haft kontakt med Tycho’. Postscript: keep the book horizontal in its capsule.
sources.role: The examiner's own record of the volume (1985–86) and the only reading of the forperm's third inscription (‘Sum Paul…’) and of the herbarium's date.

sources.label: Helsingør examination 2026
sources.full: M/S Museet for Søfart, Helsingør: the volume 1957:0030 examined and photographed at the museum's study centre on 20 October 2026, by appointment with the curator, who brought the volume, its box and the examiner's report of 2003 from the store — sixty-four photographs (both boards, the three edges and the spine with its label fragment; the front pastedown; the fly-title recto and verso; the Regiomontanus title, dedication and preface leaves with the plant names; the pages carrying reader's marks; the Apianus title, the Schema and volvelles, the German place table and fol. 53r–v with the four added places; the rear pastedown and flyleaf; the report of 2003 and the slip kept in the box; the cloth box and its lettered spine), with a written record of what they settle and what stays open. Unpublished; the photographs and the record are kept with the edition's working papers, and the museum receives a set at full resolution.
sources.role: The volume read leaf by leaf in 2026: the inscriptions on both sides of the fly-title, the purchase note and the two astronomical memoranda, the four added places, the herbarium confirmed, the labels and later marks, the accession note, the box.

sources.label: Band II transcription and hand comparison 2026
sources.full: The volume 1957:0030 of M/S Museet for Søfart read from the photographs of 20 October 2026 at full resolution on 21 October 2026: a diplomatic transcription of every inscription and annotation — both sides of the fly-title, the front pastedown's ink rule and pencil collation, the plant names, the reader's marks, the four places on fol. 53, the rear flyleaf and pastedown — with the hands labelled descriptively (A–F) and no hand attributed; and a feature-by-feature comparison of the hand of the memoranda and the fol. 53 places against the dated specimens of the Graphonomicon of Tycho Brahe (the horoscope prose of 1583, the observation narrative of 1597, the album leaf of 1599) and against the unattributed index of 1563–65 in the Uppsala volume of 1563. Unpublished; kept with the edition's working papers beside the photographs.
sources.role: The readings of the inscriptions and annotations, letter by letter; the purchase note corrected to ‘emptus thalero et 4 grossis’; the two memoranda read in full; the hand comparison and its verdicts.

sources.label: Bjørnbo & Petersen, Claudius Clavus (1904)
sources.full: Axel Anthon Bjørnbo and Carl S. Petersen, Fyenboen Claudius Claussøn Swart (Claudius Clavus), Nordens ældste Kartograf. En Monografi (Det Kgl. Danske Videnskabernes Selskabs Skrifter, 6. Række, historisk og filosofisk Afdeling VI.2; Copenhagen 1904); German edition Der Däne Claudius Claussøn Swart (Claudius Clavus), der älteste Kartograph des Nordens (Innsbruck 1909). Pp. 114–115: the synoptic table of Irenicus, Schöner and the Vienna manuscripts of Clavus's second description of the North, Schöner column ‘Gotlandia insula Suetie contermina habet gradus longitudinis 48.0. Latitudinis vero 60.0. Bespue uel wisbuy 47.5. 59.50. Rumefalche. 46.35. 60.15.’; p. 118: the names Schöner took from an A/B-type map — ‘paa Gotland: Bespue uel Wisbuy, Rumefalche’ — and the proof that his map was the Ulm Ptolemy of 1486 with Reger's Registrum. Digitised: archive.org fyenboenclaudius00bjor (1904), derdaneclaudiusc00bjor (1909).
sources.role: Establishes that Schöner's Gotland ‘cities’, Bespue and Rumefalche, are Claudius Clavus's names transmitted through the Ulm Ptolemy of 1486 — so the fourth place on fol. 53v is a pseudo-toponym, not a locality — and that the 1518 printing Bjørnbo used reads ‘Bespue uel wisbuy’.

sources.label: Schöner, Luculentissima … descriptio (1515)
sources.full: Johannes Schöner, Luculentissima quaedam terrae totius descriptio, cum multis utilissimis cosmographiae iniciis (Nuremberg: Johannes Stuchs, 1515), the text to his globe of 1515; Tractatus II, De Europae civitatibus, fo. 34r: ‘Gotlandiae insu. civita. — Bespue 47.5.59.50. Rumefalche 46.35.60.15.’, with Stocholma 42.38.60.30, Vpsalia 39.45.61.15, Roschilde 34.16.56.20, Copenhagna 35.24.56.30 on the same page. Digitised copy: archive.org luculentissimaqu00schn (leaf 100).
sources.role: The printed source of the two Gotland lines added on fol. 53v of the Apianus in the volume of 1561 — name and figures verbatim — and of the Helsingborg and Lund figures that Apian's own table repeats.

sources.label: Šolc 2018
sources.full: Martin Šolc, ‘Zum Schicksal der naturwissenschaftlichen Bibliothek von Tycho Brahe – Funde in Prag und Dresden’, in Beket Bukovinská and Lubomír Konečný (eds), *Dresden–Prag um 1600* (Studia Rudolphina, Sonderheft 2; Prague: Artefactum, Institute of Art History, Czech Academy of Sciences, 2018), pp. 191–205, with colour plates of the T.B. 1560 Sammelband (18 J 318), the Glareanus of 19 G 20, the Reinhold of 14 J 176, the Ptolemy 5 B 70, the Ziegler 7 B 27, the two Scaligers (14 A 59, 19 A 46), the Mnichovo Hradiště *De nova stella* (Sign. 40.09.07) and the SLUB Dresden *Mechanica* (S.B.14). The Clementinum specialist's account of the library's history and of the Prague and Dresden finds, with his counts (about 110 printed texts and 5 manuscripts in 52 volumes at the NKP), the Rantzau volumes in Prague and Dresden, and Falkenstein's 1839 descriptions of the Dresden Tychoniana quoted at length.
sources.role: The 2018 state of the Clementinum's Tycho holdings and the Dresden finds; the published reproductions of nine Tycho volumes; the only study since 2002 by the library's own specialist.

sources.label: Falkenstein 1839
sources.full: Constantin Karl Falkenstein, *Beschreibung der Königlichen öffentlichen Bibliothek zu Dresden* (Dresden: Walther, 1839; the preface dated September 1838), 832 pp. — the librarian's room-by-room description of the Dresden royal library. At pp. 574–575 the Tychonianum then in the library: Paulus Alexandrinus, *Rudimenta in doctrinam de praedictis natalitiis* (Wittenberg 1588, 4°), with Heinrich Rantzau's *Horoscopographia* (Wittenberg 1588, 4°) and Michael Boiemus's *Historia de somniis* (Wittenberg 1587, 4°) bound after it, two distichs by M. Johannes Schmidt on the flyleaf, addressed ‘Doctissime Smile’ and ‘Generositatis tuae’ (‘Promissum transmitto librum …’), the entry standing in the section ‘Griechische Philosophen’, in a parchment binding with Tycho's portrait stamp on the front and his arms on the back; at pp. 790–791 the two Dresden copies of the *Mechanica* (the author's dedication copy to the princes Christian, Johann Georg and August, with seven distichs, in green satin with the gilt portrait; and the illuminated copy with the autograph ‘Jo. Ad. Alberti de Fabriciis Anno 1698’ and Holger Rosenkrantz's autograph poem), Kepler's dedication copies and the Rantzau volumes. Read in the archive.org scan with its OCR; pp. 574–575 read on the page image on 29 October 2026 — the OCR's ‘Praemissum’ is the page's ‘Promissum’, and the addressee the OCR garbled is printed ‘Smile’.
sources.role: The eyewitness description of the lost Dresden Sammelband and of the two Dresden *Mechanica* copies, 1839.

sources.label: Copenhagen examination 2026
sources.full: Det Kgl. Bibliotek, Forskningslæsesalen: the volume 88, 201 01801 (eks. 2) examined and photographed on 21 October 2026 — thirty-eight photographs (both boards under several lightings, the spine with its ink title, the three edges and the endbands, the front pastedown and free endpaper, the dedication opening and the dedication at macro scale, the Calvin title under normal, raking and transmitted light, the end of the Calvin index, the Theocritus title, the rear pastedown, and ruler frames on both dies and the roll), with the written record of what they settle: docs/research/2026-10-21-kb-calvin-lindenov-autopsy-dedication-hand-marks.md (a transcription of the dedication letter by letter, a feature-by-feature assessment of the hand against the Graphonomicon's secure specimens with an adversarial refutation, the identification of every library and trade mark, the binding described and the dies measured, the two editions and their devices), and the continuation research of the same afternoon on the pre-1954 route, the binding tools, Lindenov's whereabouts in 1597–1601 and the son's album. Binding 175 × 120 × 75 mm, leaves 171 × 106 × 70 mm. Unpublished; the photographs, the working crops, the rose montage and the hand-comparison sheet are filed in the corpus folder named here, with a README that is the examination's written record.
sources.role: The volume read on the object in 2026: which copy it is, the accession and custody marks, the pre-1954 marks, the dedication's wording and hand, the binding and the dies.

sources.label: Royal Library, Opklaring af bogtyverierne (2005)
sources.full: Det Kongelige Bibliotek, *Opklaring af bogtyverierne på Det Kongelige Bibliotek. Redegørelse* (Copenhagen, 5 January 2005): the library's account of its collections, catalogues, marks and stores — the Udenlandske Afdeling's Ældre Samling and its protocol catalogue of c. 1816–30 whose signatures (two numbers with comma and dash, in pencil top left of the front pastedown) the books carry (pp. 12, 72–73); the Boghistorisk Studiesamling, c. 1,900 volumes chosen for equipment, provenance or annotations, kept in a locked store from its start in the 1950s (pp. 12, 72); the climate-controlled and secured boksmagasin in the Holm building funded by aktstykke nr. 598 of 26 July 1976 and the move of rare books into secured stores in 1977–78 (pp. 19–21); the test revisions of May–June 1977 (pp. 30–31); the stamping of acquisitions on the title from 1906 (pp. 22–23); and the rule that duplicates were not signed before they were separated (p. 51).
sources.role: The key to the library's own pencil marks in the Lindenov volume: the catalogue signature 88,-201, 'Boghist. Saml.', 'BOX', 'S-1977', the cancelled earlier location, and why a sold duplicate would carry no KB mark.

sources.label: Royal Library, Royal Identification Marks (2005)
sources.full: Det Kongelige Bibliotek, *Royal Identification Marks — shelf marks and ownership marks* (the library's missing-books site, 2005): the forms of the library's shelfmarks by collection and period — for non-Danish books up to the middle of the twentieth century two numbers separated by a comma and a dash, written in pencil, normally top left of the front pastedown — and its accession stamp 'Bibl. Reg. Hafniensis' with the accession year and a serial number.
sources.role: The form of the catalogue signature and of the accession mark.

sources.label: Royal Library archive registratur 1994
sources.full: *Det Kongelige Biblioteks Arkiv indtil 1943. Registratur* (Indsigt. Det Kongelige Biblioteks arkivregistraturer 6; Copenhagen 1994): the library's own archive — the foreign accession catalogue F 6 a (1901–50), numbered within each financial year and covering gifts as well as purchases (p. 60); the gift registers (F 60); the duplicate catalogues and the duplicate sales (E 62; 'Afgang (dubletter)', p. 72).
sources.role: The accession-numbering practice behind the pencil '1954 g. 230'; where the 1783 and 1786 duplicate catalogues sit.

sources.label: Kancelliets Brevbøger 1596–1602
sources.full: *Kancelliets Brevbøger vedrørende Danmarks indre Forhold. I Uddrag. 1596–1602*, ed. L. Laursen (Rigsarkivet; Copenhagen 1913); read in the Wikisource transcription, checked against the printed register, 21 October 2026. Hans Christoffersen Lindenov, lensmand at Hammershus: the lensbrev from 1 May 1597 (pp. 126–127), the missive of 20 June 1597 on the Swedish musters (p. 171), the Bilde complaint of 26 July 1597 (p. 187), the herredag notices to be published on Bornholm (pp. 243, 408), the new lensbrev from 1 May 1599 (p. 419), the Gæsteri letters of 12 and 15 November 1600 — 'Slotsskriveren, som nu var her med Hans Lindenovs Regnskab' (pp. 561, 563–564), the stranded munitions of 12 November 1601 (p. 684), the daler notice of 1602 (p. 740); the register names no other Hans Lindenov for these years.
sources.role: Where Lindenov was in 1597–1602: every letter reaches him on Bornholm; none summons him to Copenhagen.

sources.label: Kancelliets Brevbøger 1593–1596
sources.full: *Kancelliets Brevbøger vedrørende Danmarks indre Forhold. I Uddrag. 1593–1596*, ed. L. Laursen (Rigsarkivet; Copenhagen 1910); Wikisource transcription. Hans Lindenov: the Hammershus handover orders of 13–14 June 1594 (pp. 298, 300) and the lensbrev of 20 June 1594 (p. 306); the royal leave of 12 February 1596 'at drage fra Bornholm til sit Hjem' on condition of returning at the first opportunity (p. 585); the summons to Christian IV's coronation of 2 May 1596 (p. 626); named 'til Ødtsløf' in June 1596 (pp. 667, 670).
sources.role: The Hammershus enfeoffment of June 1594 — two weeks before the Hven visit — and the one recorded leave.

sources.label: Ilsøe 1998
sources.full: Harald Ilsøe, ‘Bøger der gik den anden vej. Om Det kongelige Biblioteks dubletsalg og -afgivelser’, *Fund og Forskning* 37 (1998), pp. 11–62, the catalogues listed pp. 55–58: the duplicate auctions of 1723 (2,555 numbers), 1742 (917; annotated copy in the library's archive E 23), 1783 (2,340; E 62), 1786 (4,477; E 62) and 1836 (10,863 numbers; *Index librorum duplorum*), the sale of 701 numbers to the Edinburgh bookseller Laing in 1800, and the gifts to Oslo 1811–13, Ålborg 1821 and Reykjavik 1827 without catalogues.
sources.role: The duplicate sales through which a Royal Library book could have left Denmark; none of the catalogues is online, and none has been searched for this volume.

sources.label: Dødsfald i Danmark 1959
sources.full: Niels Friis, *Dødsfald i Danmark i Aaret 1959* (supplement to *Personalhistorisk Tidsskrift*, 1961): ‘Bruhn, Hj., Skibsmgl., KS. 21.12.’ — the ship-broker Hjalmar Bruhn died on 21 December 1959 (Københavns Skifteret); the only ship-broker of the name in the volumes for 1957–61.
sources.role: Bruhn's death date.

sources.label: VD16
sources.full: *Verzeichnis der im deutschen Sprachbereich erschienenen Drucke des 16. Jahrhunderts* (VD16), Bayerische Staatsbibliothek, via Gateway Bayern. C 304: Calvin, *Epistolae et responsa*, editio tertia, Hanau, Wilhelm Antonius, 1597, [28] Bl., 804[=806] S., 8°. ZV 14910: Theocritus, *Eidyllia kai epigrammata / Idyllia & epigrammata* … Moschus, Bion, Simmias … *Iosephi Scaligeri & Isaaci Casauboni Emendationes seorsim dabuntur*, Heidelberg, Hieronymus Commelinus, 1596, [8] Bl., 319, 30 S., [1] Bl., 150 S., 8°, three parts, the third identical with C 1236; copies digitised at the BSB (bsb00015923, bsb10994489) and the ÖNB (*35.H.134).
sources.role: The bibliographical identity of the two constituents, read at the record 21 October 2026.
sources.url_label: Gateway Bayern, VD16 ZV 14910 (the Calvin: VD16+C+304)

sources.label: ADB, Antonius
sources.full: ‘Antonius, Wilhelm’, *Allgemeine Deutsche Biographie* 1 (1875): the Hanau printer's two devices — the earliest a winged stag with a rider holding a sickle and a crowned serpent; the later a mountain with a pelican on its summit and the motto ‘Est via invia virtuti nulla’.
sources.role: The identification of the Calvin title's device as the pelican on the mountain.

sources.label: Vaculínová 2006
sources.full: Marta Vaculínová, ‘Latinské průpovědi a citáty v památnících Knihovny Národního muzea’, *Folia Historica Bohemica* 22 (2006), pp. 111–120: the album of Tycho's son (Národní muzeum VI F 44) — Prague from September 1599, Nuremberg and Augsburg early in 1601, Bologna in March, Florence at the end of March, Siena on 26 September 1601, Prague again at the beginning of 1602, the Bohemian entries of 1603–12, Štampach's poem of 1610 (with her commentary in *Listy filologické* 121, 1998, pp. 319–322).
sources.role: The son's itinerary 1599–1612 — Italy, Prague and northern Bohemia, never Denmark after 1599.

sources.label: Národní muzeum, VI F 44 (Manuscriptorium record)
sources.full: Knihovna Národního muzea, Prague, VI F 44 — the album amicorum of Tycho Brahe the younger (1581–1627), 1598–1652, 180 ff.: the museum's catalogue description as published in Manuscriptorium — the father's dedication at Wittenberg on 28 February 1599; Danish and Swedish compatriots at Wittenberg; the imperial court circle at Prague from 8 August 1599; one Copenhagen entry of 28 October 1599, on the journey made with Tengnagel to bring the mother and siblings to Bohemia; Bologna, Florence and Siena; Prague definitively in 1602; the entries of 1603–1612 written at České Zlatníky by the wife's kin, neighbours and the pastor Wolfgang Schreiber (3 May 1611); Štampach's ‘Carmen amicitiae’ of 1610; the grandson Otto's entries at Prague 1646–52.
sources.role: The dating of the album's only Copenhagen entry to October 1599 and of every later entry to Bohemia.

sources.label: Helk 1994
sources.full: Vello Helk, ‘Stambogsstudier. Med forskningsoversigt tilbage til 1983’, *Fund og Forskning* 33 (1994): the register of alba amicorum, under Tyge Brahe the younger — 55 entries 1598–1602, 1607, 1611–12, from Augsburg, Bologna, Braunschweig, Breitenburg, Florence, Hamburg, Helmstedt, Copenhagen, Nykøbing F., Nuremberg, Prague, Siena, Wittenberg and elsewhere; continued by Otto Tyge Brahe with five Prague entries of 1646–47 and 1652; literature Studnička 1901, pp. 14–15, Mortensen, *Cassiopeia* 14 (1953), p. 99.
sources.role: The album's places and years as a union of all entries — not a dating of any one entry.

sources.label: Early European Books, LN 430 eks. 1
sources.full: Early European Books (ProQuest), the Royal Danish Library's copy of Tycho Brahe, *Epistolarum astronomicarum libri* (Uraniborg 1596), LN 430 4°, eks. 1 — the copy presented to Duke Johan Adolf of Schleswig-Holstein-Gottorp (Alma 563: ‘Grøn atlask med forgyldte borte og Brahes portræt på bindets forside; på bagsiden Brahes våben; ciseleret guldsnit’; 561: the dedication slip; 700: Johan Adolf as former owner); the one-page preview is the front cover, 1536 × 2143 px, ‘Images reproduced by courtesy of Det Kongelige Bibliotek’. The copy Gigas 1900 cited as Astr. 1100.
sources.role: The cover of the Johan Adolf Epistolae at measurable resolution: the Hven rose, c. 14 mm; the roll, 6.2–6.6 mm pitch.

sources.label: Smithsonian Libraries, Dibner Epistolae image
sources.full: Smithsonian Libraries, image gallery 108893–108894: the Dibner Library's copy of the *Epistolarum astronomicarum libri* (1596) in its Hven presentation binding, photographed with a Kodak colour and inch/cm scale (SIL-SIL28-190-01, 3194 × 4000 px, 11.83 px/mm).
sources.role: The Hven presentation rose at the best resolution available: 14.4–15.2 mm, line-hatched petals, seeded centre; the six-pointed star-in-circle, c. 13 mm.

sources.label: Kungliga biblioteket, RAR 106 A digitisation
sources.full: Kungliga biblioteket, Stockholm: the digitisation of RAR 106 A, Tycho Brahe, *De mundi aetherei recentioribus phaenomenis* (Uraniborg 1588), Dudith's copy in its Hven presentation binding — both covers and a flat front view with a centimetre ruler (157.2 px/cm) among the scans.
sources.role: The Hven presentation rose against a ruler on a binding of 1588: 14.1–14.9 mm.

sources.label: Charlier 1901
sources.full: C. V. L. Charlier, *Utgräfningarna af Tycho Brahes observatorier på ön Hven sommaren 1901*, Lunds Universitets Årsskrift 37 (1901), Afd. 2, N:o 8 (= Kongl. Fysiografiska Sällskapets Handlingar N.F. 12, N:o 8), 20 pp., 3 plates.
sources.role: The 1901 excavation record: the south wing's outer wall found, no trace of the library rotunda's inner wall (p. 7); the square 1430–1445 cm and a Tychonic foot of 23.8 cm (p. 9).

pages.via: archive.org; the Google scan of the Årsskrift volume, leaf 321.

sources.label: 5 B 70 hand comparison 2026
sources.full: The purchase note of 30 November 1560 and the marginalia of NK ČR 5 B 70 compared, on the Manuscriptorium facsimile, with the two ‘Iohannes Pratensis’ signatures on the same title page, with Tycho's dated specimens of 1583 (KB GKS 1823) and 1599 (the album leaf of 8 May), and with the two hands of the volume of 1561 at Helsingør, on 25 October 2026: the scribe-compare method (each specimen's features extracted blind, the vectors compared, every claim audited against the images), with the pipeline's three verdict bands. Every pair returned ‘inconclusive’: the note against the signatures with a weak lean against identity (the h built on different limbs, pointed against rounded minims; the shared capital I the period's standard form), against Tycho's specimens with a weak lean against (the capital I without the J-descender, the final s at x-height against his descending final s), against the hands of 1561 with a weak lean against; the marginalia against Tycho's specimens with a weak-to-moderate lean against (the u-marks and the looped g agree; the open e, the 3-shaped final s, the absence of the ſt/ct arch and the j-form final i do not — a German-cursive repertoire the secure hands show nowhere). Sample lengths below the forensic floor; the facsimile's c. 15–20 px x-height for the note is the binding constraint. Unpublished; the crops, the claims and the audits are kept with the edition's working papers.
sources.role: The hands of the note and the marginalia tested against Pratensis and against Tycho: not shown to be Tycho's, not shown to be Pratensis's; the marginalia leaning away from Tycho.

sources.label: Westman 2011
sources.full: Robert S. Westman, *The Copernican Question: Prognostication, Skepticism, and Celestial Order* (Berkeley and Los Angeles: University of California Press, 2011; first paperback printing 2020). Chapter 8 (pp. 223–258) on the nova of 1572, the Copenhagen oration and the Tychonian problematic; chapter 10 (pp. 281–300) on Wittich, the via media and the Rothmann exchange; the Clementinum volumes reproduced as figs 46–48.
sources.role: The one modern study to read two of Tycho's bindings of 1576 for their contents — the Bellanti of 14 A 66 and the Naibod of 5 J 2 — and the only printed refusal of the figure of three thousand volumes.

sources.label: Albrecht 1901–02
sources.full: F. & M. Albrecht, ‘Die Reste der Sternwarten Tycho Brahe's auf der Insel Hveen’, *Das Weltall: illustrierte Zeitschrift für Astronomie und verwandte Gebiete* 2 (1901–02), Heft 1, pp. 7–12 (Uranienburg), Heft 2, pp. 21–25 (Sternenburg), with the colour plans ‘Die Reste der Uranienburg’ and ‘Die Reste der Sternenburg’ (‘Aufgenommen am 13.
