August 1901 durch Max Albrecht. Massstab 1:160’) and two photographic supplements; F. Albrecht's review of Charlier 1901, ibid., pp. 274–276.
sources.role: The Treptow observatory's survey of the ruins in the summer of Charlier's excavation: the one measured plan that lays Tycho's ground plan over the found masonry, and the statement that the north tower's inner ring survives with a radius of about 3 m.

sources.label: Jern 1976
sources.full: Carl Henrik Jern, *Uraniborg: herresäte och himlaborg* (Lund: Studentlitteratur, 1976); pp. 37–39 the dimensions and the foot, pp. 40–47 the rooms of the house and their uses, pp. 44–45 the library.
sources.role: The architectural monograph on the house, with the critique of Beckett and Christensen's dimensions.

sources.label: Moryson 1617
sources.full: Fynes Moryson, *An Itinerary … containing his ten yeeres travell* (London: John Beale, 1617), Part I, Book I, pp. 59–60 (Denmark, 1593); reprinted Glasgow 1907, vol. I, pp. 125–127.
sources.role: The only visitor's text that names the library.
sources.url_label: archive.org — the Glasgow reprint, vol. I

sources.label: Beckett & Christensen 1921
sources.full: Francis Beckett (text) and Charles Christensen (measured drawings), *Tyge Brahes Uraniborg og Stjærneborg paa Hven* (Copenhagen, 1921), Tavle 1–9: Tavle 2 the ground floor at 1:200, Tavle 4 the north–south section through the south tower at 1:150.
sources.role: The reconstruction drawings; the section gives the vault's springing used for the shelving.

sources.label: Friis 1871
sources.full: F. R. Friis, *Tyge Brahe. En historisk Fremstilling efter trykte og utrykte Kilder* (Copenhagen, 1871), pp. 104–105.
sources.role: The first Danish synthesis of the room, with its own figure for the diameter.

sources.label: Sjökvist 2024
sources.full: Peter Sjökvist, *Looted Libraries, Looted Books: The Swedish Case* (Brill Research Perspectives in Humanities and Social Sciences; Leiden and Boston: Brill, 2024). The Swedish book plunder of the seventeenth century as a whole: p. 35, the Danish war of 1658–60, in which Magnus Gabriel De la Gardie ‘acquired … big parts of the collections of Gunde Rosenkrantz (1604–1675), in which large portions of books previously owned by Holger Rosencrantz (1574–1642) and Anders Sörensen Vedel (1542–1616) could be found’; p. 64, the Stockholm castle fire of 1697, which destroyed about three quarters of the royal library's holdings, the Bohemian spoils among them.
sources.role: The mechanism the Uppsala volume of 1563 lacked — Vedel's books as a body into De la Gardie's hands — and the likeliest grave of the Tengnagel manuscripts of 1648.

sources.label: Šípek 2014
sources.full: Richard Šípek, *Die Jauerer Schlossbibliothek Ottos des Jüngeren von Nostitz*, Teil 1–2 (Frankfurt am Main: Peter Lang, 2014). The catalogue of the Nostitz library: p. 62, no. 167, a work of Tycho's (Heidelberg: Voegelinus; G 233); p. 651, a volume with the note ‘… Monauio Ticho Brahe dono misit’ — a presentation copy Tycho sent to Jakob Monau; p. 662, the Wittich entries (452390–452392).
sources.role: What the Nostitz library actually holds of Tycho: his own works and his gifts to Monau, and Wittich's books — the likeliest base of Friis's hearsay of 1868, not books from Tycho's library.

sources.label: Muszyński 1977
sources.full: Michał Muszyński, ‘Proweniencje poloników XVI wieku w zbiorach Biblioteki Kórnickiej (uzupełnienia do Katalogu K. Piekarskiego)’, *Pamiętnik Biblioteki Kórnickiej* 13 (1977), pp. 145–270. Entry 583 (p. 182): Heidenstein, De bello Moscovitico, Basel 1588, Cim.Qu.2812 — ‘Collegii Societatis Jesu Commotorii catalogo inscriptus a. 1671. 2. Z Hankowych [piecz.]. 3. [A. T. Działyński-kat. Kiel.]’; the index (p. 253) reads the stamp as Václav Hanka's (1791–1861), citing Encyklopedia Gutenberga 6, p. 86, and lists it on nos. 583, 584 (Heidenstein, German, Görlitz 1590, Cim.Qu.2813 adl., earlier ‘Conventus Virginis Annuntiatae Neo-Pragae’) and 1022 (Oderborn, Görlitz 1589, Cim.Qu.2814 adl.); p. 147 on the Kielisiński mark and the later purchase lists.
sources.role: The Kórnik cataloguer's reading of the stamp and the terminus ante quem of the Heidenstein's arrival.

sources.label: Bolewska (Kielisiński)
sources.full: Bolewska, ‘Trudy bibliotekarskie K. W. Kielisińskiego w Kórniku (1840–1849)’, *Pamiętnik Biblioteki Kórnickiej* 15, pp. 66–67: Kajetan Wincenty Kielisiński's card catalogue of Tytus Działyński's old prints, begun 1840, c. 10,000 works, the chronological cards ending in 1847.
sources.role: Dates the ‘kat. Kiel.’ mark in Muszyński's entries.

sources.label: NK ČR record STT 000005829
sources.full: Národní knihovna ČR, base STT (STT01), system no. 000005829: Bianchini, Tabulae, Venice 1526. ‘Ex Bibliotheca Tichoniana’ on the title; ‘Collegii Caesarei Soc[ieta]tis IESV Pragae A[nn]o 1642’; ‘na patě původní klementinská signatura S.IV.41’; Teplá's stamps, the label ‘Bibl. Can. Tepl. C107’ and ‘C.IV.37’ on the front pastedown; ‘přírůstkové číslo 07/ORST 394’; Hlinomaz's catalogue of postincunabula no. 136. Read 27 October 2026.
sources.role: The holder of the Bianchini of 1642 is the National Library, the Teplá marks being those of a former owner.

sources.label: Boldan c. 2013 (Teplá)
sources.full: Kamil Boldan, a report on the National Library's acquisition of the Teplá monastery's manuscripts, incunabula and paleotypes (c. 2013; free PDF at kba.vkol.cz; the title to be completed from the file), p. 35: the Library bought the fond ‘teprve před několika lety’, its core in 2006 and 2007 — the ‘07/’ of the accession number.
sources.role: Dates the Teplá purchase.

sources.label: Thiermann 1927
sources.full: Thiermann, ‘Abendmahlsgänge Altdorfer Studierender nach Oberferrieden und Leinburg …’, *Zeitschrift für bayerische Kirchengeschichte* 2 (1927), pp. 21–31; the lists on pp. 28–30 (archive.org item zbkg-1-3) name among the Altdorf students at communion at Christmas 1599 ‘Daniel Crusius Bohemus, Studiosus juris’ (matriculated 1598, ‘von Görkau’) and ‘Gabriel Crusius von Görgau, Studiosus Juris’.
sources.role: A Gabriel Crusius of Jirkov who was Daniel's fellow student — brother or kinsman, not son.

sources.label: Garwoliński 2008
sources.full: Garwoliński, *Fides* 1–2 (26–27) (2008), pp. 59–72 (bazhum PDF): the Braunsberg seminary and State Academy burned in 1945; p. 68, of the rescued old prints ‘Przewieziono jednak tylko książki z sygnaturami De i Fb’ — only the theology and church-history shelfmarks, with single copies of other classes, went to Olsztyn, the rest ‘probably’ to the University Library at Toruń by the correspondence of 1946.
sources.role: Where the Braunsberg Scaliger of 1598 would be, if it survived: Toruń rather than the Hosianum.

sources.label: SLUB war-loss register
sources.full: Sächsische Landesbibliothek – Staats- und Universitätsbibliothek Dresden, Nachweiskatalog der Kriegsverluste (kriegsverluste.slub-dresden.de): card image 00504111 — Boiemus, Historia … ad Henr. Ranzovium, Witebergae 1587, 4°, shelfmark Lit.Graec.B.1976, earlier ‘Phil. gr. B. 93a. Misc. 3’. No card found under Paulus Alexandrinus or the Horoscopographia (searched 27 October 2026).
sources.role: The one archival trace of the Dresden Sammelband's loss.

sources.label: SBL (Hierta)
sources.full: Lindberg, ‘Per Hierta’, *Svenskt biografiskt lexikon* 19, p. 32 (SBL id 13576): Hierta's collection of bookbindings, ‘framför allt från renässansen’, is the core of the Röhsska's bindings and was given to the museum by Hjalmar Wijk in 1915; *Nordisk familjebok*, 4th ed., p. 528: Wijk bought ‘P. Hiertas saml. av bokband’. Hierta d. 1924.
sources.role: The road of Hierta's bindings to the Röhsska, and the staleness of Prandtl's 1932 placing.

sources.label: Svobodová 2022
sources.full: Svobodová, *Acta Musei Nationalis Pragae – Historia litterarum* 67 (2022), p. 39 and n. 10 (on the Hibernian library, dissolved 1786): at the Clementinum Ungar ‘vytřídil duplikáty a knihy považované za bezcenné, ty byly rozprodány nebo skončily jako makulatura’; a larger part of the discards was bought by Strnad through a Jewish antiquarian; the rest scattered to the National Museum library, the City of Prague Museum and castle libraries (after Seydl and Kouklová).
sources.role: A second description of Ungar's discards and the Strnad purchase.

sources.label: Newberry (Karr Schmidt 2023)
sources.full: Karr Schmidt, Newberry Library digital collections blog, 3 March 2023 (dcc.newberry.org/?p=21137): the Silver Apianus ‘was never accessioned, and was sold to help defray the costs of the Silver sale’.
sources.role: The Newberry's own account of lot 4 of 8–9 November 1965.

sources.label: Kašparová, Mašek, Měřička & Šípek 2022
sources.full: Jaroslava Kašparová, Petr Mašek, Vlasta Měřička & Richard Šípek, *Fragmenty českých knižních sbírek v evropských knihovnách* (Prague: Národní muzeum, 2022): p. 8 and pp. 22–23 (the Wrocław university library's historical tie to the Nostitz majorat library; 105 of the 158 owners excerpted at Wrocław from the Nostitz survey); pp. 24–25, three Tycho volumes in the BUWr provenance index — 461815 Epistolae astronomicae 1596 dedicated to Jakob Monau, later the Hospital of St Matthias 1640; 461816 De mundi aetherei II 1588 dedicated to Johannes Praetorius 18 September 1588; 461817 the same with a note ‘Pragae … Julij 1599’, later Scheibel — ‘strictly speaking’ gifts, Uraniborg imprints.
sources.role: What Wrocław holds of Tycho: his gifts, not his library.

sources.label: Bruun Rasmussen 186 (1965)
sources.full: Katalog over Ingeniør Oscar Ekmans og Fru Lia Ekmans Bogsamling, Auktion nr. 186 (Copenhagen: Branners Bibliofile Antikvariat and Arne Bruun Rasmussen Kunstauktioner, 1965; sale 1–4 November 1965, Bredgade 33), p. 111, lot 497, under the heading ‘En Bog fra Tycho Brahe's Bibliotek’: Regiomontanus, Tabulae directionum (Tübingen 1550), bound with Apianus, Cosmographia (Paris 1553), ‘i et samtidigt bind med Tycho Brahe's navn og årstal 1561’ — ‘Eksemplaret er kun optaget i kataloget for fuldstændighedens skyld; den er blevet foræret til Handels- og Søfartsmuseet på Kronborg af ingeniør Ekman og kan beses der i en af udstillingsmontrerne. This copy will not be sold as it was given to the “Handels- og Søfartsmuseet” at Kronborg according to the last will of ingeniør Ekman.’ A copy in a private collection, read and photographed 29 October 2026.
sources.role: The sale catalogue's own statement that the volume of 1561 was Oscar Ekman's bequest to the museum, not sold, and on display at Kronborg in 1965.

size_debate.summary: The library’s original size is unresolved: the estimates run from Mortensen’s ceiling of 1,000 volumes to Christianson’s ‘over three thousand’, and the higher figure rests on a single shelf-number.

positions.basis: the shelf-number 2781 that Studnička read in 1901 on the spine of [[vol:s-band-xxi|the Gesner of 1565]], now in Austin, where the spine shows no number; reported by Norlind

‘similar numbers are apparently not found in the other surviving volumes, so Norlind’s deduction is at best speculative’; nevertheless a library of 3,000 titles ‘would not be unreasonable’ beside Rantzau’s 6,000 and Dee’s about 4,000

what the circular Museum room at Uraniborg, 5 m across and also holding the great globe and the smaller instruments, could have held, and the argument that a larger library would have left more survivors: ‘Forsigtig tør man maaske sætte Antallet af Bind til højst 1000 svarende til omkring 2000 Skrifter’

the figure Mortensen printed without attribution in 1942, p. 25 (‘Tallet har vel naaet circ. 5000 Bd.’), gave in 1955, p. 31, as Walde’s estimate in a private letter of 1938, and judged probably too large (‘vistnok for stort’): it would need more room than the Museum had, and more books would have survived

size_debate.note: Norlind himself wrote that it is impossible to form any estimate of the library’s size, crediting the 2781 inference to Studnička (Norlind 1970, p. 335).

events.label: Tycho Brahe born at Knutstorp
Procures the Ephemerides of Stadius after the eclipse of 21 August — the first book of Dreyer’s account, and the ‘few books, particularly ephemerides’ of Tycho’s own; no copy survives

Sacrobosco’s Libellus de sphaera (Wittenberg 1558), Bayrus’s Enchiridion (Basel 1560) and Macer’s herbal (Basel 1559) bound in blind-stamped pigskin lettered ‘T. B. 1560’ (Prague, NK ČR 18 J 318) — the earliest dated binding attributed to Tycho, on the cipher alone — no inscription, no annotation, no note of 1642, the one Tycho volume from the Jesuit professed house (ownership C since 29 October 2026)
events.source: Kleinschnitzová 1933, no. 47; Christianson 1967, pp. 200–201; Šolc 2018, figs 1a–c

events.label: The Prague Ptolemy (Basel 1551) bought at Copenhagen for 2 thaler by Johannes Pratensis, whose name and 1561 binding it carries — Dreyer’s reading of the note as Tycho’s own, repeated from Friis to Šolc 1999 without a comparison, has no positive support (the hands compared 2026); Tycho’s later, probably from Pratensis’s estate after 1576 (ownership B since 29 October 2026)
events.source: Dreyer 1890, p. 14; Friis 1868–69, p. 267; Studnička 1901, p. 39; Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 74; Boldan & Vackářová 2024, pp. 144–145; the hand comparison of 25 October 2026

events.label: Regiomontanus’s Tabulae directionum (Tübingen 1550) and Apianus’s Cosmographia (Paris 1553) bound in calf stamped ‘TVCHO BRADE’ and ‘ANNO 1561’, bought for a thaler and four groschen — the earliest purchase note, beside an ownership entry in Tycho’s name; the one surviving volume documented as Tycho’s before he left Denmark on 14 February 1562, the place of purchase an inference from the year (Helsingør, M/S Museet for Søfart 1957:0030)
events.source: Prandtl 1932, Band II; Museernes Samlinger 1957:0030; Christianson 1967, p. 201

events.label: To Leipzig to read law; buys astronomical books and instruments with money accounted for to his tutor
‘Ty Brad 1563’ sammelband (later gifted to Vedel; now Uppsala)
events.source: Prandtl 1932, Verz. B, Band III; Mortensen 1955, p. 27

events.label: The Strahov Euclid (Basel 1558) bound with TYCHO / BRAHE 1567 stamped on the board — the latest of the three dated name-stamps of the student years (after TVCHO BRADE 1561 and TY BRAD 1563) and the only one in the spelling BRAHE

Tycho has several copies of the Prutenic Tables bought at his own expense and distributed to the poorer students at his Copenhagen lectures — ‘Curaueram autem coëmi proprio ære aliquot exemplaria tabularum Prutenicarum’
events.source: TBOO I 173 (the appendix to the Oratio de disciplinis mathematicis, first printed 1913); Thoren 1990, p. 86

events.label: An attempt to buy the books of Dr Ambrose, a citizen of Augsburg, fails
Granted Hven; Uraniborg begun; the T.B.O. 1576 binding cohort
events.source: Prandtl 1932, Heft 8; Norlind 1970, p. 335; Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 81

events.label: An attempt, through Camerarius, to buy Brechtalius’s mathematical books: already sold
Marks 13 titles in a Frankfurt fair catalogue for procurement
Gives Wittich the Apian Astronomicum Caesareum (departure gift)
First book from the Uraniborg press: Morsing’s Diarium astrologicum for 1586, its dedication dated 1 January 1586 (the first imprints, the poems to Pratensis and Ulfeldt, are of late 1584)
The engraved portrait dated 1586, from which Mortensen derived the supralibros portrait stamp
Tycho learns of Wittich's death (from Rothmann)
Bruno's Camoeracensis acrotismus received (author gift)
Earliest dated binding with the gilt supralibros portrait: the Sascerides De mundi (KB Copenhagen)
First attempt to buy Wittich’s library, through noble emissaries at Wrocław, fails
Seeks Rheticus’s and Copernicus’s papers from Hagecius
Second attempt to buy Wittich’s library, through Hagecius and Monau, fails
The whole library inventoried on Hven (‘all the junker's books’)
events.source: Friis (ed.) 1876, p. 263; TBOO IX, p. 146; Thoren 1990, p. 371

events.label: Tycho leaves Hven for the last time: 29 March on Dreyer’s reading of the observing ledger’s ‘29 Aprilis’ (Easter fell on 27 March), followed by Thoren; Nielsen keeps 29 April
events.source: Dreyer 1890, p. 238 n. 2; Thoren 1990, p. 371; Nielsen 1921, p. 204

events.label: Departs Copenhagen into exile
Tycho has bought four copies of the Rheticus–Otho Opus Palatinum (1596) before Landgrave Moritz presents a fifth — ‘cuius quidem antea quaterna exemplaria coëmeram’
events.source: TBOO XIV 105–108 — Tycho to Moritz, Rostock, 17 June 1597 (epistolarium brahe-t_15970617001); VIII 386–388

events.label: At Wandsbek with Rantzau; the travelling press prints the Mechanica
Third attempt, through Longomontanus and Monau: the library found intact; negotiation opens
Winter at Wittenberg
Kepler's Mysterium cosmographicum arrives (with Ursus's tract)
Enters Rudolf II's service; assigned Benátky castle
The library, shipped up the Elbe and held at Magdeburg since 1599, reaches Prague in mid-November

At Benátky, Baron Karl von Wartenberg shows Tycho the catalogue of the whole library of the late Andreas Dudith; Tycho keeps it to return on a visit to the baron's castle ‘seven miles’ away and asks Monau whether the heirs would let him see, and sell, the books he had marked
events.source: TBOO VIII, 320.37–321.5 — Tycho to Jacob Monau, Benátky, 16 May 1600 (epistolarium brahe-t_16000516001); Mosley 2007, p. 175, nn. 281–282

events.label: Monau answers that Dudith's library ‘now hangs as if between heaven and earth’ — no longer the heirs', ‘not so much sold as pawned’ to another for a sum of money — and the pursuit ends; the Dudith copy of the De mundi that survives at Stockholm is Tycho's gift of 1588, not a purchase
events.source: TBOO VIII, 325.39–326.6 — Jacob Monau to Tycho, Wrocław, 14 June 1600 (epistolarium brahe-t_16000614001); Mosley 2007, p. 175, n. 283

events.label: Monau in Prague (his attestation of 23 October); the Wittich Copernicus copies presumed, not documented, to have come with him — no letter records a price, a payment or a delivery
events.source: Gingerich 2002, p. 325 (‘presumably’); Gingerich & Westman 1988, p. 22 (‘the end of the story’); Monau to Tycho, 14 June 1600, TBOO VIII 325–326

events.label: Tycho Brahe dies at Prague; the library remains with his heirs
Kepler named imperial mathematician (charged with the manuscripts and instruments)

The sale to Rudolf II is dated by the king's own bond of 1614 to ‘the end of the year 1601’: Matthias acknowledges owing the six children 15,000 kop míšeňských ‘for some rare astronomical instruments and books left by their father and bought from them at the end of 1601’ (‘za některá vzáctná instrumenta astronomická a knihy … při konci léta 1601 koupené’), of which 4,000 were paid in 1603 and 1,000 in 1604; the word is ‘knihy’ — the observation books in the house's reading, the bond itself not saying which books

The family, and with it the library, leaves Curtius's house for the Old Town before July 1602 (Magdalene Brahe to Eske Bille, Danske Magazin II, p. 361 ff.); a year or two before her death in 1604 the widow buys a country property towards the Saxon frontier, where the elder son marries in March 1604 — the heirs' orbit after 1602 is the Old Town and the Saxon border, the Chomutov side of Bohemia

The heirs — Tengnagel with Elisabeth, Tycho and Jørgen — assign 2,000 thaler of the purchase money to Bernhard Fürst, burgher of Kiel, Tengnagel's creditor, who cedes the claim to Jan Rebeník of the Malá Strana; Rudolf orders the first 4,000 thaler paid on 23 September 1603 (receipted by Tycho and Jørgen on the 25th, Tengnagel not signing); Rebeník asks on 14 October that the heirs be gaoled until paid, and on 13 April 1604 Tengnagel pleads that he has pawned all he could and borrowed 800 thaler anew — the heirs' first documented sales of their possessions
events.agent: the heirs; Bernhard Fürst; Jan Rebeník

events.label: Of the 20,000 thalers Rudolf II agreed to pay for the instruments and manuscripts, only 4,000 paid

The instruments ‘cum libris observationum’ moved to Vienna on Rudolf II’s order, ‘for greater safety’, according to Kleinschnitzová; Dreyer keeps the instruments in Prague, in a vault under Curtius’s house, until their destruction in 1619, and has the observation books pass to Kepler under his contract with Tengnagel of 1604; the library itself stays with the heirs

Matthias's bond to the six heirs for the 15,000 kop outstanding, payable at St George 1615 and 1616 with 6,312 kop of interest in five terms — never honoured; the heirs' name is absent from the Diet's debt schedule of 1615, and the war of 1618 follows

After the White Mountain the Protestant heirs must in time leave Bohemia — Dvorský gives no date, and Georg and Rudolf Tycho were still in Prague in November–December 1624 (KGW XIX nos. 9–10): ‘Kam se uchýlili, nevíme’ — where they went, Dvorský could not say (the children's later papers place them in Bohemia and Saxony); only Tengnagel, councillor of appeal and convert, remains, dying 1 December 1622 — where the library stood between 1620 and 1642 is undocumented
Tengnagel dies; the book-dispersal accelerates
A Brahe book already in private hands (Budějovice)

The heirs' claim on the Bohemian Chamber is assigned to the tax arrears of four royal towns — Žatec (1,000 thaler), Kadaň (1,000), Rakovník (950) and Chomutov (950) — the instructions to the towns to pay from their arrears dated Chomutov 26 September 1623 and Kadaň 3 July 1626 — and the towns, unable to pay, send small instalments until 1654: a documented tie between the heirs and the two towns of the second Jesuit road and of Sophie Brahe's bequest; whether it carried books is undocumented
Kepler urges Georg Brahe to have a careful catalogue made of all that remains of Tycho's library in books and manuscripts, and asks for the Greek Hipparchus with Scaliger's hand

Ferdinand II allows one creditor of the Brahe heirs to come to Prague; the family sends Jørgen (Tycho the younger having died 2 September 1627); the reformation commissioners press him weekly to leave, and through the 1630s he goes every half year to Rakovník and to Chomutov to collect the interest on the towns' arrears — a Brahe heir on the road to Chomutov in the years before the first dated Tycho accession there (1645); his sister Sophie joins him during the Saxon invasion of 1631 and later turns Catholic

Ferdinand II orders part of the interest on the 70,000 thaler granted by the Diet paid to the heirs; the Saxon invasion of the same month stops the payment. In the same invasion the Chomutov college, which the Jesuits had left before the occupation, is plundered and its library confiscated — valued by the Jesuits at 10,000 gulden, the soldiers' sale realising 100 — and partly bought back in 1632; Banér holds the town in 1639, Wrangel takes it in 1645 and 1647: the Tycho volumes first dated there in 1645 entered a library being rebuilt after plunder
events.source: Volf 1932, part 2, p. 24; Veselá 2025, pp. 27–29 (Schmidl 1754, p. 119; the NK survey of 2021 in n. 71)
events.agent: Ferdinand II; the Saxon army; the Chomutov Jesuits

events.label: A Musaeum mathematicum exists at the Clementinum: the Ryff Sammelband NK 14 E 3 is inscribed ‘Collegii Caesarei Soctis JESU Pragae Musaei Mathem: A.1638’ — the institution the Tycho books joined four years later

Jørgen Brahe, the heir who had pursued the debt in Bohemia, dies below Křivoklát after his last visit to Rakovník; his Rakovník bond passes by will to Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel, imperial councillor, reformation commissioner and from 1642 captain of the Malá Strana — the family's Prague presence in the year of the Clementinum gift is now a Catholic grandson and a Catholic daughter
events.agent: Jørgen Brahe; Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel

events.label: The surviving core passes to the Jesuit college in the Clementinum, Prague (‘A. 1642’) — a gift according to Volf, Kleinschnitzová and Šolc, a purchase from the heirs according to Tobolka
events.source: Šolc 2002, p. 329; Kleinschnitzová 1933, pp. 76–78; Volf 1932, part 2, p. 24; Fabian, Handbuch (Prague), §1.13

events.label: The Opus palatinum and a Regiomontanus now at Strahov receive the Jesuit inscription with the rest of the core

In the year of the Clementinum gift Sophie Brahe bequeaths her claim on the Chamber to the Franciscans of Kadaň (15,000 fl. by Dvorský; 9,942 fl. by Volf) and Rudolf Tycho Tengnagel cedes his mother Elisabeth's share to the Dominicans of St Giles (17,500 fl. by Dvorský; Ferdinand III's assecuration of 14 March 1643 for 22,534 fl. by Volf): the heirs' three gifts to religious houses of 1642–43 are of one piece
events.agent: Sophie Brahe; Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel

events.label: Ferdinand III's assecuration to the Dominicans of St Giles, Prague, for 22,534 fl. 22 kr. 4 d. — Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel's share of the heirs' claim, given to the convent (Arch. min. vnitra, Bekennen u. Verträge 1642/65); Sophie Brahe's share (9,942 fl.) went the same way to the Franciscans of Kadaň, and both houses were paid in iron in 1672: in the year after the Clementinum gift the heirs were giving their claims, as they had given their books, to religious houses
events.agent: Rudolf Tycho Gansneb Tengnagel; Sophie Brahe

events.label: The incunable Sammelband 44 F 38 (d’Ailly’s Imago mundi and the Ratdolt Euclid of 1482, bound 1576, with Tycho’s monogram) is entered in the catalogue of the Jesuit college at Chomutov — the earliest dated Chomutov accession of a Tycho volume, unless the note on 14 B 11, read 1675 by Kleinschnitzová and Šolc and 1645 by the library’s cataloguer, is also of 1645
The Swedish capture of Hradčany and the Malá Strana; the Rudolfine collections carried to Sweden (26 July 1648 New Style; 16 July Old Style)

The Castle’s books removed before 8 October and the Kunstkammer on 1–2 November; shipped in casks by the Vltava and the Elbe to Dömitz, then Wismar, reaching Stockholm at the end of May 1649 — two Tycho manuscripts and a Tycho print of Rudolf II’s collection among them
Vossius’s recataloguing of the Stockholm royal library (1650–51) enters the two Tycho manuscripts under Frans Tengnagel’s name and strips the booty’s spine marks
events.source: Veselá 2025, pp. 142 n. 494, 208–214; Vossius–Callmer 1971, p. 19 no. 2 and p. 18 no. 4

events.label: The last archival word on the heirs: the reformation commissioners report from the Brandýs nad Orlicí estate that Otto Tycho Brahe, the astronomer's grandson and an imperial Wachtmeister, explains at Těchlovice why his sister Kristina Barbara von Salhausen has stayed six years in Bohemia against the imperial order — she came with the Elector of Saxony's safe-conduct to collect the debt; Rakovník's envoys pay Tengnagel 35 kop on account on 9 November 1654
events.agent: Otto Tycho Brahe; Kristina Barbara von Salhausen

events.label: Crusius gives two Tycho volumes to the Chomutov Jesuits
Christina abdicates; takes loot (incl. a Tychonic Copernicus) to Rome
Ludwig Kepler sells the observation-originals to Frederick III (Copenhagen)
events.source: Mortensen 1955, pp. 31–32 (Dreyer 1890, Appendix, p. 373: by early 1662 at the latest)

events.label: The Vienna set of observation copies in the Hofbibliothek by about 1657
The Museum's formal foundation under the rector Retz, with the astronomical tower; Caspar Pflieger first prefect (1722/23–1729/30)
events.source: Seydl 1951, pp. 1–3; Mačák 1995/96, pp. 74–75 (Fischer 1978 for Pflieger, p. 74; Retz and the tower p. 75, the link offered as a possibility, n. 8 = Seydl 1938)

events.label: The Jesuit suppression reunites the Chomutov/Krumlov fragments at the Clementinum
Strahov buys the library of Jan Josef Klauser — Tycho’s Euclid comes with it, without any Jesuit mark

The anonymous Neue Chronik von Böhmen (Prague: Schönfeld 1780, ‘Beschreibung der Hauptstadt Prag’, pp. 65 and 88) sends whoever wants to see the Museum's collections to the university librarian, then Karel Rafael Ungar — a statement Seydl sets against Strnad's own petition of 1782 to the court study commission, which recalls the raises promised him in 1778, 1780 and 1781 ‘because he voluntarily took over the professorship and because he administers the museum’; Seydl's reading: the librarian received the visitors, the astronomer kept the collections

At Karel Rafael Ungar's cataloguing of the 1780s the Tycho volumes are placed in the University Library's thematically corresponding departments, predominantly department 14 — Šolc's sequence of division, moving and loss after 1778; he does not say what the first element of a present shelfmark denotes

The Mathematical Museum dissolved as a whole, the University Library needing its rooms for the books of the suppressed monasteries; its portrait prints had gone to the library in 1781, when Strnad's list of its contents still ended with ‘some books’
Antonín Strnad dies; Strahov buys the substantial part of his library, into which Clementinum surplus had passed after 1773

By c. 1847 the Heidenstein of 1588 (Cim.Qu.2812), inscribed by the Chomutov college in 1671, stands in Kielisiński's catalogue at Kórnik with Václav Hanka's red stamp — the one Chomutov volume known to have left Bohemia, by way of Hanka's Prague
Friis surveys the Tychonic manuscripts in Vienna and Prague

Count Franz von Klebelsberg, descendant of Rudolf Tycho Tengnagel's daughter, gives the Bohemian National Museum a collection of books and manuscripts concerning the Brahe and Tengnagel families, the Stammbuch of 1598 among them; no printed book from Tycho's library is named in the gift
events.source: Mortensen, ‘Tycho Brahe Minder i Prag’; Mitteilungen des Österr. Vereins für Bibliothekswesen 5 (1901), pp. 51–52

events.label: Šafařík distributes photolithographs of the standing-Tycho watercolour in the Házmburk Progymnasmata at Strahov
Prusík lists the Clementinum Tychoniana after the recataloguing: four manuscripts and sixteen printed works in four groups by binding

Kukula counts five manuscripts and fifty printed works in twenty-eight volumes, seven of them found since 1902; Ludwig Rosenthal's Zwinger volume with the plaques is published in the same number, and Bargum answers that its binding is Danish work
events.source: Kukula 1906–07, pp. 17–25; ZfB 1906–07 (binding note), pp. 42–43; Bargum 1906–07, pp. 124–126

events.label: Straka publishes the weather note in the Strahov Regiomontanus and attributes it to Tycho's hand

Hjalmar Wijk gives Per Hierta's collection of bookbindings to the Röhsska museum, Göteborg — most probably the road of the Zwinger with Tycho's plaques, which Prandtl still placed at Hierta's Främmestad in 1932, eight years after Hierta's death
events.source: SBL 19, p. 32; Nordisk familjebok, 4th ed., p. 528

events.label: Norlind's first list from the letters: thirty-two printed works, the unprinted writings and the loans that Tycho's own statements place on Hven
Prandtl publishes the first printed catalogue of the library
Kleinschnitzová’s census of the Clementinum Tychoniana: 97 works in 47 volumes

Walde publishes the Braunsberg copy of Scaliger's De emendatione temporum (Leiden 1598) in blind-stamped parchment with the plaques, and the books of Tycho's amanuensis Johannes Eriksen in Queen Christina's library

Felix Mainx prints a three-page notice on the Strahov library: its original editions of Copernicus, Tycho Brahe and Kepler ‘from the possession of the Prague astronomer A. Strnad’, two Stammbücher with entries of Melanchthon and of Brahe, and no supralibros volume — three years before his report of the eight volumes
events.source: Mainx 1940, printed pp. 41–43 (scans 2–4); the Tycho sentences printed p. 43 (scan 4)

events.label: Mortensen's intermediate count: 110 works in 57 volumes (the 47 Clementinum volumes with those at Göteborg, Braunsberg, Dresden, Gotha and Mnichovo Hradiště, the Mainx, Prandtl and Mortensen volumes, the Uppsala Sammelband of 1563 and the volume of 1561), superseded in 1955 by 67 volumes with 121 works
Mainx reports eight supralibros volumes in a Prague monastery; they have not been traced since

The Dresden Sammelband (Paulus Alexandrinus 1588 – Rantzau 1588 – Boiemus 1587, in Tycho's parchment with his plaques) is lost: the SLUB's war-loss register carries the Boiemus under Lit.Graec.B.1976 (earlier Phil. gr. B. 93a. Misc. 3), removed in 1945–46 or destroyed, the card not saying which
events.source: SLUB Nachweiskatalog der Kriegsverluste, card 00504111; Norlind 1970, p. 356
Handels- og Søfartsmuseet, Årbog 1957; Prandtl 1932, pp. 2–3; Mortensen 1942, p. 25
events.label: Oscar Ekman’s bequest of the Regiomontanus–Apianus volume of 1561 (Prandtl’s Band II), entered in January 1957 by his widow Lia and listed in the sale of their library in 1965 as not for sale, sold by Weiss & Co. of Munich to America in 1932, to the Handels- og Søfartsmuseet på Kronborg

The Wittich Apianus (Tycho's gift of 29 October 1580) is sold at Sotheby's, London, in the Newberry Library's Silver-duplicates sale of 8–9 November 1965, lot 4, to Warren Howell for Joseph Halle Schaffner; Rundetaarn's ‘very high but vain’ bid on ‘a similar’ Tycho-library book at Sotheby's that month (Dal, Bogvennen 1966, p. 205) this lot is the candidate for that bid — no bidding record seen
Norlind publishes his reconstructed catalogue of the library (Bilaga I) and reports Studnička’s shelf-number 2781

The Clementinum Copernicus of 1566 (14 B 16) is the centrepiece of Prague's Copernicus quincentenary exhibition, still shown as Tycho's annotated copy; Horský's facsimile of 1971 serves the year, and at a conference in Paris Horský hands it to Gingerich, who recognises in it the hand of the Vatican copy — the reattribution to Wittich follows in 1981–88
events.source: Vackářová 2026, printed pp. 8–10 and 31–32 (scans 8–10, 31–32); venue and organiser of the exhibition not named; the Paris year is her implication, not her statement

events.label: Björklund reports the volume of 1561 deposited by the museum at the Royal Library’s manuscript department
Šolc recounts the Clementinum holdings (about 110 titles in 50 volumes); Gingerich publishes the dispersed survivors he found

The National Library buys the Teplá monastery's manuscripts, incunabula and paleotypes (the core in 2006 and 2007): the Bianchini of 1642 that had left the Clementinum for Teplá returns to it, accession 07/ORST 394
events.source: NK ČR record STT 000005829; Boldan c. 2013, p. 35

events.label: Pařez publishes the Strahov supralibros, including the Basel Euclid of 1558 in its binding stamped 1567, found by Kuchařová

Šolc's count: about 110 printed texts and 5 manuscripts in 52 volumes at the National Library in Prague; at least five volumes beyond Kleinschnitzová's 47 now listed; Gingerich's 16 volumes with T.B.O. on the board, 6 with the portrait supralibros and 12 with the written initials; Westman's 33 volumes with ‘T.B.O. 1576’ in various libraries; Norlind's 216 titles from the letters and the extant volumes; further Tychonic volumes at Mnichovo Hradiště and in the SLUB Dresden

Boldan and Kazanskii publish the incunable Sammelband 44 F 38 with Tycho's monogram and glosses, unknown to Kleinschnitzová: the first Tycho volume found in the National Library's incunable collection

‘Bibliotheca astronomica’, the National Library's exhibition in the Galerie Klementinum, 18 October – 18 December 2024, with the catalogue by Boldan & Vackářová, whose ninth chapter (pp. 86–100) is on Tycho's library
Boldan's census of Ratdolt's astronomica joins the Strahov Regiomontanus (DR VII 19) to the National Library's 1481 Ephemerides: two halves of one book from Tycho's library

acquisition_channels.name: Frankfurt book fair
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Standing orders through the biannual Willer catalogues, executed by correspondents who bought at the fair to order.

acquisition_channels.name: Procured by a correspondent or agent
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Books bought to order or procured on request by a correspondent and sent on — Johannes Maior's parcel from Augsburg (June 1584), Paul Hainzel's comet tracts (March 1579), Heinrich Brucaeus's sendings from Rostock (March 1586, June 1584) — as distinct from purchases made at the Frankfurt fair itself (AQ-FAIR). Norlind grouped the four men as the intermediaries of Tycho's purchases (1970, p. 333); the channel is split so that a book bought at the fair and a book found for him by a friend are not one thing.

acquisition_channels.name: Absorbed scholar-libraries
acquisition_channels.mechanism: The pursuit of a dead scholar’s whole working library — Ambrose (1575), Brechtalius (1576), Dudith, Wittich (1589–1598); only the Wittich pursuit is thought to have succeeded, in part — the annotated De revolutionibus copies presumed delivered in October 1600, without a documented price, payment or receipt.

acquisition_channels.name: Gift of an author or correspondent
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Presentation copies from authors and correspondents.

acquisition_channels.name: Manuscript copying and transmission
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Manuscript copies made of texts he could not buy, and the search of other libraries for them (Vedel).

acquisition_channels.name: Direct purchase
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Books bought outright, often with an autograph purchase-note.

acquisition_channels.name: Borrowed, not owned
acquisition_channels.mechanism: Some fifty mathematical titles lent from the Duke of Bavaria’s library through Herwart in the Prague years — used, never owned, and so outside this catalogue.

mark_chronology.mark: The name stamped on the boards — TVCHO BRADE / ANNO 1561 ([[vol:s-band-ii|Helsingør]]), TY BRAD 1563 ([[vol:s-band-iii|Uppsala]]), TYCHO / BRAHE 1567 ([[vol:s-strahov-av-ii-2|Strahov AV II 2]]) — and the initials alone with the year, T. B. 1560 ([[vol:s-kl-47|18 J 318]]) and 1567 ([[vol:s-kl-44|10 G 47]]) (Kleinschnitzová 1933, nos. 47, 44)
mark_chronology.indicates: Student purchases, all before Hven: Copenhagen, Leipzig, Rostock. The two Prague volumes are the only dated bindings of the student years in the Clementinum (Kleinschnitzová 1933, nos. 44, 47) Only the Helsingør volume of 1561 is dated before Tycho’s departure from Denmark on 14 February 1562; the bindings of 1563 and 1567 belong to the Leipzig and Rostock years, and the cipher T. B. 1560 is unverified (ownership C, 29 October 2026).

mark_chronology.mark: Brown leather with the cipher T.B.O., no year reported (Prusík 1901, group B; Prandtl 1932, Verz. B XII–XV)
mark_chronology.indicates: Prandtl’s second period, after Prusík 1901, who reported the cipher without a year; Kleinschnitzová read ‘T. B. O. 1576’ on every volume Prandtl placed here, so no located volume is now assigned to it

mark_chronology.mark: Brown calf, a narrow gilt border, a rhomboid arabesque at the centre, T.B.O. above it and the year beneath — mostly 1576, also 1580 and 1582 (Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 81), and 1583 (Gingerich 2002, fig. 2) Šolc's description of the type (2006, printed p. 191 (scan 5); 1999, § 2.530): up to six thinner prints of one format bound together in brown leather, the initials TBO — which he expands ‘Tycho Brahe Otonensis’ — the year 1576, 1580 or 1582, and four small stars in the corners; his sentence puts the gilt portrait and arms into the same type, which conflates it with the supralibros bindings of period 4.
mark_chronology.indicates: Books bound when Uraniborg was being furnished (Prandtl 1932, p. 11). Where they were bound is not settled: a binder on Hven according to Prandtl (p. 9), a Copenhagen workshop sharing Vedel’s stamps according to Kleinschnitzová (p. 82)

Presentation copies and selected library books; six of the Clementinum volumes (Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 81: 8 H 39, 12 H 10, 14 G 30, 14 J 176, 19 C 92, 9 B 135) Šolc (2006, printed p. 191 (scan 5); 1999, § 2.530) counts ‘seven books’ in richly decorated white parchment with gilt arms at the centre, some of them masterpieces of Renaissance binding; Kleinschnitzová's six supralibros volumes (p. 81) comprise two in brown calf (8 H 39, 12 H 10) and four in white parchment (14 G 30, 14 J 176, 19 C 92, 9 B 135), and his seven are not reconciled with her list — the volumes added since 1933 may account for the difference.
Gifts and copies received ready-bound, not stamped by Tycho’s binder; eight Clementinum volumes carry only the handwritten ‘T. B.’ (Kleinschnitzová 1933, p. 81)

mark_checklist: An oval gilt portrait medallion on the upper board, with the distich ‘Hic patet exterior Tychonis forma Brahei…’, in two sizes — about 76 × 58 and 58 × 43 mm, as measured in the table below — indicates a presentation binding of period 4, Prandtl’s Prachtband (1932, p. 11).
The arms oval on the lower board, with ‘Arma genus, fundi pereunt; durabile virtus…’, accompanies the portrait.
The gilt cipher T.B.O. on brown calf with a rhomboid arabesque and the year beneath indicates period 3; the same cipher with no year reported is Prandtl’s period 2.
Handwritten ‘T. B.’ initials or a purchase-note on the title-page mark gifts and copies received ready-bound.

The Jesuit accession inscription ‘A. 1642 / Ex Bibliotheca Tychoniana’, or a Chomutov, Krumlov or professed-house catalogue entry (Chomutov 1645–1675, two of them Crusius’s gifts of 1654), indicates the Jesuit road — the Clementinum, or a Jesuit house whose library came to it after 1773.
history.mark_chronology_note: The dies of period 4 are dated by the presentation copies of De mundi (1588): the Sascerides copy, Royal Danish Library LN 428 4° ex. 1, its dedication dated 20 March 1588 (Norlind 1970, p. 122; [[census:brahe-de-mundi-1588|the census of De mundi]]); the Scultetus copy at Görlitz, portrait and arms, dedication dated 8 May 1588 (Norlind 1970, p. 124); the Maestlin copy in the British Library, dedication dated 14 May 1588 (Norlind 1970, p. 122).

die_measurements.measured_on: the Vienna observation quartos, Cod. 10657–10675: the last five carry the large stamps, the first twelve the small; two have simpler vignettes
the Royal Danish Library’s Calvin–Theocritus volume carries the small die
Strahov Σ V 5/a and AG XIV 7 (the large die), Σ VI 3 (the small)

die_measurements.source: the volumes examined at Strahov, 18 September 2026

die_measurements.large: about 80 × 60 mm, against a ruler in the photographs
